title: Quantum Control Geometry As A Metric Of Chaos
authors: Joaquin F. Rodriguez-Nieva Mahmoud Abdelshafy
abstract: ArXiv:2611.13101v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum-chaotic systems share the same coarse-grained features characteristic of random matrices, such as Wigner-Dyson level-spacing statistics, yet can exhibit strikingly different eigenstate structure and many-body dynamics, including relaxation, transport, scrambling, and entanglement growth. This raises the fundamental question of whether these finer-grained features probe genuinely distinct aspects of quantum chaos or, instead, reflect different manifestations of a common underlying structure---and whether such structure provides a meaningful basis for regarding one many-body quantum system as "more chaotic" than another. Here, we address this question by introducing a quantum geometric framework that quantifies the susceptibility of many-body eigenstates to physically allowed deformations of the Hamiltonian, as constrained by spatial locality, symmetries, and conservation laws. The resulting geometric susceptibility is quantitative, providing a metric of chaos beyond traditional binary diagnostics; intrinsic, as it depends on the manifold of allowed Hamiltonian deformations rather than on the way the system is probed; and unifying, as it directly connects eigenstate structure with dynamics. For canonical models of quantum chaos, we find that minimal geometric susceptibility, maximal eigenstate randomness, broad spectral response of local operators, and the suppression of nonhydrodynamic slow structure coalesce in the same region of Hamiltonian control space. This suggests that these seemingly distinct signatures of chaos are different manifestations of a common underlying geometric structure. Our framework provides a route toward understanding the limits of relaxation and scrambling under physical constraints; in applications, it offers a means to engineer strongly chaotic regimes in programmable quantum systems with restricted controls.
tldr: The paper introduces a quantum-geometric susceptibility of many-body eigenstates to Hamiltonian deformations as a quantitative metric of quantum chaos.
motivation: Quantum-chaotic systems share random-matrix spectral statistics but can differ in eigenstate structure and dynamics, raising the question of whether there is a unified, quantitative notion of 'more chaotic' many-body systems.
method: The authors define a geometric susceptibility measuring eigenstate sensitivity to physically allowed Hamiltonian deformations constrained by locality, symmetries, and conservation laws, and compare it with spectral and dynamical chaos diagnostics in canonical models.
result: They find that minimal geometric susceptibility, maximal eigenstate randomness, broad local-operator spectral response, and suppressed nonhydrodynamic slow structure coincide in the same region of Hamiltonian control space.
conclusion: The framework suggests that distinct signatures of quantum chaos may stem from a common geometric structure and offers a route to engineering strongly chaotic regimes in programmable quantum systems with restricted controls.

title: Quantum Simulation Of Real-time Bosonic Dynamics With Binary And Unary Position Encodings On Superconducting And Trapped-ion Processors
authors: Masanori Hanada, Jiwoo Seo, Seok-Kyun Son, Junggi Yoon
abstract: ArXiv:2611.13079v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Simulating a bosonic degree of freedom on qubit hardware requires discretizing its position space, and the qubit encoding of the resulting lattice determines the circuits that realize its real-time dynamics. We compare binary and unary encodings of a position lattice on superconducting (IBM) and trapped-ion (IonQ) processors. Binary encoding applies the kinetic term through the quantum Fourier transform; unary encoding uses one qubit per site, single-qubit rotations for the potential and excitation-conserving exchange gates for the kinetic term. For a single degree of freedom the unary dynamics is a free-fermion problem, and its product formula compresses exactly into a nearest-neighbor circuit of fixed size. With about two hundred two-qubit gates, these circuits resolve tunneling in a symmetric double well on both processors, with the right-well probability falling from 0.97 to 0.06 on IBM and from 0.96 to 0.12 on IonQ, whereas binary product-formula circuits with several thousand two-qubit gates do not reproduce the transfer. Noiseless emulation indicates that this contrast reflects the compilation as well as the encoding: without the fixed-size optimization, a unary product formula that captures the transfer also requires several thousand two-qubit gates. Post-selection on the single-excitation subspace removes leakage, and because every energy eigenstate of the symmetric grid populates both wells equally, the measured population reversal bounds the coherence between energy eigenstates from below. Coupled-oscillator benchmarks, where inter-register interactions prevent this exact compression, show that the preferred encoding depends on the grid size and the evolution time.
tldr: The paper compares binary and unary qubit encodings for real-time bosonic dynamics on IBM superconducting and IonQ trapped-ion processors, finding that optimized unary circuits resolve double-well tunneling with far fewer two-qubit gates than binary product-formula circuits.
motivation: Simulating a bosonic degree of freedom on qubit hardware requires discretizing position space, and the chosen encoding strongly affects circuit depth, gate count, and near-term hardware feasibility.
method: The authors implement binary encoding using the quantum Fourier transform for the kinetic term and unary encoding using one qubit per lattice site, single-qubit rotations for the potential, and excitation-conserving exchange gates for the kinetic term, then benchmark both on superconducting and trapped-ion processors with post-selection on the single-excitation subspace.
result: Optimized unary circuits with about two hundred two-qubit gates resolve tunneling in a symmetric double well on both processors, with right-well probability dropping from 0.97 to 0.06 on IBM and 0.96 to 0.12 on IonQ, whereas binary circuits with several thousand two-qubit gates do not reproduce the transfer; noiseless emulation shows the contrast depends on compilation as well as encoding.
conclusion: Unary encoding can be advantageous for single-bosonic-mode simulation on near-term hardware due to exact circuit compression, but for coupled oscillators the preferred encoding depends on grid size and evolution time.

title: An Efficient Quantum Algorithm For Preparing Uniform Superpositions Over Arbitrary Integer Intervals
authors: Prakash Vedula Alok Shukla
abstract: ArXiv:2611.13658v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider exact preparation of the uniform quantum state supported on an arbitrary nonempty interval of integer labels in an [MATH]-qubit register. For every [MATH], we give an ancilla-free circuit using only one-qubit gates and singly controlled one-qubit gates. In the logical gate model specified in the paper, the direct construction has exact worst-case gate count [MATH] for [MATH]; its exact maxima for [MATH] and [MATH] are [MATH] and [MATH], respectively. A worst-case lower bound of [MATH] establishes asymptotic optimality in the register width. In addition, the gate complexity admits an instance-dependent bound [MATH], where [MATH] is an offset-dependent parameter defined in terms of binary Hamming weights. We also derive a reflected construction and a classical procedure that selects the lower-count exact circuit. The direct construction admits an [MATH] logical-depth upper bound. We also treat bitwise-XOR images of intervals and arithmetic progressions with power-of-two spacing.
tldr: The paper gives an ancilla-free exact quantum circuit for preparing uniform superpositions over arbitrary integer intervals, with gate-count and depth bounds.
motivation: Uniform superpositions over arbitrary intervals are a basic state-preparation primitive for quantum algorithms, and exact resource-efficient circuits are useful for implementation.
method: The authors construct circuits using one-qubit gates and singly controlled one-qubit gates, prove worst-case and instance-dependent gate-count bounds, and derive a reflected construction plus a classical procedure to select the lower-count exact circuit.
result: The direct construction is asymptotically optimal in register width, admits a logarithmic-depth upper bound, and is extended to bitwise-XOR images of intervals and arithmetic progressions with power-of-two spacing.
conclusion: This is a technically solid quantum circuit synthesis/state-preparation result, but it lies outside the core information-theoretic, thermodynamic, network, and hybrid-systems focuses.

title: Rational Quantum Spectral Filtering By Repeat-until-success Protocol
authors: Maksim A. Gavreev, Aleksey K. Fedorov, Evgeniy O. Kiktenko
abstract: ArXiv:2611.13154v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a finite-memory repeat-until-success (RUS) framework for implementing rational spectral filters on a quantum computer, extending spectral filtering beyond the polynomial transformations implemented by quantum signal processing (QSP) and quantum singular value transformation (QSVT). Our approach interleaves queries to a block encoding of a Hermitian operator [MATH], whose spectrum lies in [MATH], and mid-circuit measurements that either accept, reject, or continue the computation without resetting the quantum state. Although the protocol may run for arbitrarily many rounds, its terminal statistics are determined by a finite-dimensional Lyapunov equation. Under uniform termination and phase-inversion symmetry, we characterize exactly the spectral filters [MATH] realizable upon acceptance: [MATH] can be any real rational function with no poles on [MATH] and values in [MATH]. We provide a constructive compiler for any admissible [MATH], with bounds on memory and expected query cost, and characterize the accepted quantum operation through a spectral coherence kernel. Applications to regularized resolvents and Lorentzian spectroscopy yield exact low-degree realizations and query-cost advantages over the fixed-depth QSVT polynomial-postselection baseline considered here, with all repetitions and independent restarts after rejection included in the cost.
tldr: Introduces a finite-memory repeat-until-success framework for implementing rational spectral filters on a quantum computer, extending QSP/QSVT beyond polynomial transformations.
motivation: Quantum signal processing and quantum singular value transformation can implement polynomial transformations, but many useful filters such as regularized resolvents and Lorentzians are rational functions, requiring a new protocol with rigorous resource bounds.
method: The protocol interleaves queries to a block encoding of a Hermitian operator with mid-circuit measurements that accept, reject, or continue without resetting; terminal statistics are governed by a finite-dimensional Lyapunov equation, and under uniform termination and phase-inversion symmetry the realizable filters are exactly real rational functions with no poles on the spectral interval and values in [0,1].
result: The authors give a constructive compiler for any admissible rational filter with memory and expected query-cost bounds, characterize the accepted operation via a spectral coherence kernel, and show exact low-degree realizations with query-cost advantages over a fixed-depth QSVT polynomial-postselection baseline for regularized resolvents and Lorentzian spectroscopy.
conclusion: Repeat-until-success spectral filtering expands the class of implementable spectral transformations to rational functions with finite memory and favorable query costs, enabling applications such as resolvent regularization and Lorentzian spectroscopy.

title: Double-quantum Enhanced Coherent Control And Magnetic Sensing Of Spin Defects In Hexagonal Boron Nitride
authors: Shihao Ru, Abdullah Rasmita, Jiakai Chen, Yuzhe Yang, Xiaodan Lyu, Robert Cernansky, Edwin Hang Tong Teo, Jes\'us Z\'u\~niga-P\'erez, Fedor Jelezko, Weibo Gao
abstract: ArXiv:2611.13447v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The negatively charged boron vacancy ([MATH]) in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) is a promising spin defect for quantum sensing in two-dimensional material systems. Previous hBN experiments have mainly exploited the two spin-triplet ground-state single-quantum transitions separately. Here we implement a double-quantum driving scheme based on simultaneous resonant microwave excitation of both ground-state single-quantum transitions, establishing coherent control of the [MATH] manifold in a [MATH] ensemble. We compare the resulting double-quantum response with the corresponding single-quantum protocol under identical experimental conditions. The double-quantum protocol enhances the optical readout contrast and yields a 2.6-fold signal-to-noise improvement in AC magnetometry. We further use the double-quantum relaxation channel as a differential probe of electric-field and strain noise, showing that the present data are compatible with correlated-surface or volume-distributed fluctuations, while short-range uncorrelated surface-noise models are disfavored within the assumptions of our analysis. These results establish double-quantum coherent control and frequency-resolved AC magnetometry in hBN spin ensembles, and identify the sample-dependent measurements needed to determine the microscopic origin of the dominant relaxation channels.
tldr: The paper demonstrates double-quantum coherent control of negatively charged boron vacancy spin defects in hexagonal boron nitride and uses it to improve AC magnetometry and probe electric-field/strain noise.
motivation: The boron vacancy defect in hBN is a promising platform for quantum sensing in two-dimensional materials, but prior work mostly used separate single-quantum transitions rather than simultaneous double-quantum driving.
method: The authors simultaneously drive both ground-state single-quantum transitions of the spin-triplet manifold in an hBN spin ensemble and compare the double-quantum response with a single-quantum protocol under identical experimental conditions.
result: The double-quantum protocol enhances optical readout contrast and provides a 2.6-fold signal-to-noise improvement in AC magnetometry; the double-quantum relaxation channel is also used to distinguish correlated surface/volume noise from short-range uncorrelated surface noise.
conclusion: The work establishes double-quantum coherent control and frequency-resolved AC magnetometry for hBN spin ensembles, while identifying sample-dependent measurements needed to clarify dominant relaxation mechanisms.

title: Early State Exclusion For $5\times5$ Jacobi Matrices
authors: Anastasiia Minenkova Jasmin G. Enriquez
abstract: ArXiv:2611.13315v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we present a problem that arose from quantum computing, when the quantum state to be transferred completely vanishes before the first occurrence of the perfect state transfer. It was posed as an open problem for 1D quantum chains with [MATH] of qubits, where [MATH] is an odd number. We present the solution for [MATH]. The proofs are accessible to students who studied trigonometry and calculus. As for the set-up the knowledge of eigentheory and inner products from linear algebra is needed.
tldr: The paper solves a specific open problem on early state exclusion for 5×5 Jacobi matrices arising from perfect state transfer in odd-length one-dimensional quantum chains.
motivation: Perfect state transfer in quantum spin chains is a basic quantum-information primitive, and an open problem asked whether the transferred state can vanish before the first perfect transfer for odd numbers of qubits.
method: The authors analyze 5×5 Jacobi matrices using eigentheory, inner products, trigonometry, and calculus to characterize early state exclusion in the n=5 case.
result: They provide an accessible proof resolving the n=5 instance of the open problem.
conclusion: The work settles a narrow mathematical case but does not provide a general solution for arbitrary odd-length chains or broader quantum-network protocols.

title: The Optimal Constant For One-Shot Channel Simulation And Strong Functional Representation Lemma
authors: Cheuk Ting Li
abstract: ArXiv:2611.13397v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a tight bound for one-shot channel simulation via a stronger version of the strong functional representation lemma: for any random variables [MATH], there exists a random variable [MATH] with [MATH] and [MATH], where [MATH] and [MATH] is the Euler-Mascheroni constant. A more convenient bound is [MATH]. The first bound is notable in the sense that the constant term [MATH] is optimal, and cannot be improved for any bound stated only in terms of [MATH]. Hence, this is the tightest form of the strong functional representation lemma up to the third order. We also prove that the Poisson functional representation is almost optimal up to a constant gap, and provide a simple finite-blocklength achievability bound that implies the [MATH] redundancy of the simulation of memoryless non-singular channel. These are proved via a generalization of the functional information, in particular, the exponential functional information, which closely approximates the cost of one-shot channel simulation.
tldr: The paper proves an optimal constant in a strengthened functional representation lemma, yielding tight one-shot channel simulation bounds up to third order.
motivation: One-shot channel simulation and the strong functional representation lemma are central to finite-blocklength information theory, but existing bounds leave a constant-factor gap.
method: The author generalizes functional information to exponential functional information and uses Poisson functional representation to derive improved achievability and optimality bounds.
result: The main bound contains the Euler-Mascheroni constant as an optimal constant term, the Poisson functional representation is shown to be almost optimal up to a constant gap, and a simple finite-blocklength achievability bound recovers logarithmic redundancy for memoryless non-singular channels.
conclusion: This settles the tightest form of the strong functional representation lemma up to third order and sharpens one-shot channel simulation guarantees.

title: Microscopic Derivation Of The Classical Kms Condition For One-dimensional Bose Gases
authors: Zied Ammari, Shahnaz Farhat, S\"oren Petrat, Andrew Rout
abstract: ArXiv:2611.13124v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Kubo--Martin--Schwinger (KMS) condition provides an intrinsic characterization of thermal equilibrium, both in quantum and classical statistical mechanics. In this work, we establish stability of the KMS condition through the quantum-to-classical limit for one-dimensional defocusing Bose gases. More precisely, we consider scaled quantum KMS states in the (mean-field) semiclassical regime and prove that every associated Wigner measure satisfies the classical KMS condition corresponding to the nonlinear Schr\"odinger Hamiltonian. This result extends to an infinite-dimensional setting an earlier derivation of the classical KMS condition for finite-dimensional Bose--Hubbard systems. It also provides a complementary perspective on the derivation of nonlinear Gibbs measures from many-body quantum statistical mechanics.
tldr: The authors prove that scaled quantum KMS states of one-dimensional defocusing Bose gases converge, in the mean-field semiclassical limit, to Wigner measures satisfying the classical KMS condition for the nonlinear Schrodinger Hamiltonian.
motivation: The KMS condition characterizes thermal equilibrium intrinsically in both quantum and classical statistical mechanics, but it was unclear whether this characterization survives the quantum-to-classical limit in infinite-dimensional bosonic systems.
method: Rigorous mathematical analysis of scaled quantum KMS states in the mean-field semiclassical regime, using Wigner measures to pass to the classical limit and extending finite-dimensional Bose-Hubbard results to an infinite-dimensional setting.
result: Every Wigner measure associated with the scaled quantum KMS states is shown to satisfy the classical KMS condition corresponding to the nonlinear Schrodinger Hamiltonian, giving a complementary route to derivations of nonlinear Gibbs measures.
conclusion: The KMS condition is stable under the quantum-to-classical limit for 1D defocusing Bose gases, linking many-body quantum equilibrium states to classical nonlinear Schrodinger thermal states.

title: Computational Power Of Clifford And Ising Quantum Computers
authors: Zhenghan Wang Sawyer Dobson
abstract: ArXiv:2611.13347v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We extend the efficient classical simulation of Ising quantum computers from braidings to measurements. We investigate several different definitions of efficient Clifford quantum computation by varying the power of the circuit generator. In case the circuit generator can see the entire input, we give a detailed proof that efficient simulation of classical computation would imply the separation of complexity classes [MATH] and [MATH]. If the circuit generator sees only the input length, we prove that Clifford quantum computers decide what we call affine languages.
tldr: The paper characterizes the computational power of Clifford and Ising quantum computers, extending efficient classical simulability from braidings to measurements and relating Clifford computation to complexity-class separations and affine languages.
motivation: Clifford circuits and Ising anyon braiding are known to be classically simulable, but the exact boundary of this simulability — especially under measurements and different notions of circuit generation — was not fully pinned down.
method: The authors analyze several definitions of efficient Clifford quantum computation by varying the power of the circuit generator, using complexity-theoretic reductions and algebraic characterizations of Clifford/Ising circuit families.
result: If the generator sees the entire input, efficient simulation of classical computation would imply a separation of complexity classes; if it sees only the input length, Clifford quantum computers decide exactly the affine languages.
conclusion: The work sharpens the complexity-theoretic classification of Clifford and Ising quantum computation, showing that simulability claims are sensitive to the definition of the circuit generator.

title: Euclidean Hulls Of Double Cyclic Codes Of Arbitrary Block Lengths
authors: Awadhesh Kumar Shukla, Om Prakash Pandey, Sachin Pathak, Ashish Upadhyay
abstract: ArXiv:2611.13481v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Gao et al. recently explored the Euclidean hulls of double cyclic codes over [MATH]. While they found answers for non-separable codes with coprime lengths ([MATH]), the non-coprime case ([MATH]) remained an open question. This paper completely solves that problem for all possible block lengths. We calculate the exact generator polynomials for the hull and show the precise conditions needed for a non-separable code to turn into a separable one. Using this, we show how to construct non-separable LCD codes. We also include several numerical examples to confirm our findings.
tldr: The paper determines Euclidean hulls of double cyclic codes over finite rings/fields for arbitrary block lengths, including non-coprime cases, and constructs non-separable LCD codes.
motivation: Previous work by Gao et al. solved the Euclidean hull problem for double cyclic codes only in the coprime length case; the non-coprime case remained open.
method: The authors compute exact generator polynomials for the Euclidean hull and derive precise conditions for non-separable double cyclic codes to become separable.
result: They completely solve the non-coprime block-length case, provide conditions for separability, and show how to construct non-separable LCD codes with numerical examples.
conclusion: The work closes an open problem in classical coding theory and provides constructions of LCD codes, but it is not directly connected to quantum information or quantum coding.

title: Boundary-controlled Irreversible port--Hamiltonian Modeling And Structure-preserving Discretization Of Tubular Reactors
authors: Weijun Zhou
abstract: ArXiv:2611.13421v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents a boundary-controlled irreversible port-Hamiltonian model and a structure-preserving spatial discretization for a non-isothermal tubular reactor with axial convection, variable-density momentum dynamics, chemical reaction, mass diffusion, heat conduction, and jacket heat transfer. Reaction, diffusion, and heat conduction are described by irreversible port-Hamiltonian channels, whereas convection and momentum are represented by a weighted Eulerian interconnection. The boundary ports recover the axial energy flux and the corresponding entropy flux. A partitioned finite-element method is then formulated in conservative coordinates using a power-preserving change of variables. The semi-discrete model satisfies the Hamiltonian balance and a discrete entropy balance with non-negative entropy production due to reaction, diffusion, heat conduction, and jacket heat transfer. Numerical results for an open tubular reactor are validated against independently computed continuous steady boundary-value solutions and show the transient temperature, composition, and velocity profiles in the very-low-Mach regime. The same discretization is also tested with reciprocal Soret--Dufour coupling, for which the discrete entropy production remains non-negative.
tldr: The paper develops a boundary-controlled irreversible port-Hamiltonian model and structure-preserving discretization for non-isothermal tubular reactors with coupled reaction, diffusion, and heat transfer.
motivation: It aims to provide thermodynamically consistent modeling and numerical methods for tubular reactors where reaction, diffusion, conduction, convection, and momentum dynamics are coupled.
method: Reaction, diffusion, and heat conduction are modeled as irreversible port-Hamiltonian channels, while convection and momentum use a weighted Eulerian interconnection; a partitioned finite-element discretization is formulated in conservative coordinates.
result: The semi-discrete model satisfies Hamiltonian and discrete entropy balances with non-negative entropy production, and numerical results are validated against continuous steady boundary-value solutions, including reciprocal Soret-Dufour coupling.
conclusion: The work offers a structure-preserving thermodynamic modeling framework for classical tubular reactor systems, but it is not directly aligned with quantum information thermodynamics or information-theoretic research interests.

title: Third-Order Asymptotics For Fixed-Length Lossy Compression Of Discrete Memoryless Sources
authors: Vincent Y. F. Tan
abstract: ArXiv:2611.13573v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper determines the third-order asymptotics of the logarithm of the minimum codebook size for fixed-length lossy compression of discrete memoryless sources. For an excess-distortion probability constraint [MATH] and every interior distortion level, we establish a third-order correction of [MATH], where [MATH] is the blocklength. This sharpens the general bounds of Kostina and Verd\'u [IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory, 2012]. The main technical innovation lies in the converse for positive dispersion. Under a reverse change of measure, we retain the exponential weights associated with tilted information and distortion slack and control them jointly using the multivariate weighted-strip estimate of Scarlett, Martinez, and Guill\'en i F\`abregas [Proc. IEEE ISIT, 2015]. A pairing argument verifies the required covariance nondegeneracy uniformly over all reconstruction words whose distortion balls meet a typical set, yielding the matching converse.
tldr: The paper derives third-order asymptotic corrections for fixed-length lossy compression of discrete memoryless sources under excess-distortion constraints.
motivation: It aims to sharpen existing finite-blocklength bounds of Kostina and Verdú by determining the precise third-order term in the logarithm of the minimum codebook size.
method: The analysis uses a converse argument for positive dispersion, a reverse change of measure, joint control of exponential weights via a multivariate weighted-strip estimate, and a pairing argument to verify covariance nondegeneracy.
result: For every interior distortion level and excess-distortion constraint, the logarithm of the minimum codebook size has a third-order correction involving the blocklength, improving prior general bounds.
conclusion: This provides a sharper asymptotic characterization of classical lossy source coding, but it does not address quantum information-theoretic settings.

title: Cyclically Covering Subspaces And Additive Perfect Codes
authors: Pingzhi Yuan Yangcheng Li
abstract: ArXiv:2611.13044v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be the largest codimension of a subspace of [MATH] whose cyclic shifts cover the whole space. For [MATH], we characterize the inequality [MATH] in terms of cyclic [MATH]-linear codes over vector alphabets with covering radius one, no nonzero word of block weight one, and a scalar dual generated by the shifts of one word. For [MATH], let [MATH] count the monic irreducible polynomials of degree [MATH] over [MATH]. If [MATH] is prime or [MATH], we prove that a cyclic [MATH] linear perfect code of length [MATH] over [MATH] exists if and only if [MATH]. When this condition holds, we also obtain \(h_q\!\left(-1}{q^k-1}\right)=k(m-1).\) Restriction of scalars gives the same criterion for every [MATH] when [MATH] is odd, [MATH] is a power of two, and [MATH] with [MATH] prime. We also show that [MATH] exactly when [MATH] is even, for every [MATH].

motivation: Cyclically covering subspaces and additive perfect codes are classical objects in coding theory; the authors aim to determine exactly when cyclic q-linear perfect codes of length (q^m-1)/(q-1) exist.
method: Combinatorial and algebraic techniques: characterization of a codimension inequality via cyclic F-linear codes with covering radius one and block-weight constraints, plus counting of monic irreducible polynomials over finite fields and restriction of scalars.

title: $\mathsf{SVP}_\infty$ Is NP-Hard For Power-of-two Cyclotomic Ideals
authors: Yansong Feng, Jiaqi Liu, Hengyi Luo, Yanbin Pan
abstract: ArXiv:2611.14334v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that exact decision-[MATH] in the coefficient [MATH]-norm is [MATH]-complete for principal ideals and free modules of rank two over the cyclotomic rings [MATH], where [MATH] ranges over powers of two. For each case, we give a deterministic polynomial-time many-one reduction from the Subset Sum problem. For an instance with [MATH] positive input integers, the output lattice has dimension [MATH]. A solution to the original Subset Sum instance can be recovered in polynomial time from any nonzero output lattice vector of norm at most the specified bound. We also transfer these reductions from [MATH] to the power-of-two cyclic rings [MATH]. This gives [MATH]-completeness of decision-[MATH] in the coefficient [MATH]-norm for principal ideals and free modules of any fixed positive rank over these rings.
tldr: The paper proves that the exact decision version of SVP in the coefficient infinity-norm is NP-complete for principal ideals and free modules over power-of-two cyclotomic rings, via deterministic polynomial-time reductions from Subset Sum.
motivation: Lattice problems over cyclotomic rings underpin practical post-quantum cryptosystems, so establishing the worst-case hardness of exact SVP in the coefficient norm over these structured rings clarifies the complexity-theoretic footing of ring-based cryptographic assumptions.
method: Deterministic polynomial-time many-one reductions from Subset Sum to exact decision-SVP in the coefficient infinity-norm are constructed, yielding output lattices of dimension linear in the number of input integers; solutions are recovered from short lattice vectors, and the reductions are transferred from power-of-two cyclotomic rings to power-of-two cyclic rings.
result: Decision-SVP-infinity is shown NP-complete for principal ideals and free modules of rank two over power-of-two cyclotomic rings, and extended to free modules of any fixed positive rank over the corresponding cyclic rings.
conclusion: These hardness results give strong complexity evidence for exact coefficient-norm SVP in structured rings relevant to post-quantum cryptography, complementing existing worst-case to average-case reductions for ring lattices.

title: Observation Of Strong Electric Dipole-dipole Interactions Between Two Atoms
authors: Yu-Kun Lu, Jiahao Lyu, Wolfgang Ketterle
abstract: ArXiv:2611.13665v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We have prepared pairs of atoms at densities exceeding [MATH] corresponding to [MATH] and studied how they interact with light. In this regime, the coherent part of the electric dipole-dipole interaction is larger than the dissipative part, and a single photon emission can transfer large momenta (larger than ten times the single photon recoil) to the atoms. For off-resonant laser light, the atoms are dressed with an electric dipole moment of [MATH] 1 Debye and interact coherently. This light-induced dipole-dipole interaction has been previously observed only in the far-field mean-field regime. For two atoms, the resonance is shifted by the two-body Lamb shift which is dominated by the near-field part of the dipolar interaction. Dipolar resonance shifts have been observed before only for many atoms interacting with the far-field part of the dipolar interaction. Our work sheds new light on photoassociation processes and paves the way for studying driven quantum systems with strong electric dipole-dipole interactions.
tldr: The paper reports observation of strong electric dipole-dipole interactions between pairs of atoms at high density, including coherent light-induced dipolar coupling and a two-body Lamb shift dominated by near-field interactions.
motivation: The authors aim to explore the regime where coherent dipole-dipole interactions exceed dissipative effects and to observe near-field dipolar resonance shifts that have previously been accessible only in many-atom far-field mean-field settings.
method: They prepare dense pairs of atoms and study their interaction with light, measuring photon-emission momentum transfer and off-resonant laser dressing that induces electric dipole moments.
result: They observe coherent light-induced dipole-dipole interactions with a dressed dipole moment of about 1 Debye, large momentum transfer exceeding ten recoil momenta, and a two-body Lamb shift dominated by near-field dipolar coupling.
conclusion: The work provides new insight into photoassociation and strong dipolar interactions in driven atomic systems, opening prospects for studying driven quantum systems with strong electric dipole-dipole interactions.

title: Hysteresis And Mode Switching In Fib Engineered Random Laser Diodes
authors: Andrea Mart\'inez Pacheco, Sara Rodr\'iguez Corvillo, Alberto Rivera-Calzada, Antonio Consoli, Jacobo Santamar\'ia, Cefe L\'opez
abstract: ArXiv:2611.13328v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Complex dynamical behavior in laser diodes is commonly induced by external perturbations such as optical or optoelectronic feedback and optical injection. The structural transformation of a stable laser diode into a stand-alone nonlinear dynamical system would provide a practical alternative as a single and compact device. Here we demonstrate the fabrication of such a device by milling, via focused ion beam, the output facet of a Fabry-Perot laser diode with a predesigned mask, obtaining a scattering surface which provide feedback for random lasing. The fabricated random laser diode shows multi-mode emission with current dependent spectral reconfigurations, hysteresis in output power and spectrum and mode switching at constant bias current. We attribute this behavior to the interplay between scattered optical feedback and carrier induced local variations of refractive index and temperature at the output facet surface, where defects are located. The observed phenomena reveal complex nonlinear behavior emerging from a single standalone device, which could be tailored by varying the milling pattern, thereby providing a flexible platform for different applications.
tldr: The paper demonstrates a standalone random laser diode fabricated by focused-ion-beam milling of a Fabry-Perot laser facet, showing hysteresis and mode switching due to scattered optical feedback.
motivation: The authors aim to create complex nonlinear laser dynamics in a single compact device without external optical feedback or injection.
method: They mill a predesigned scattering pattern into the output facet of a laser diode using a focused ion beam, producing random-lasing feedback, and characterize its spectral and power behavior versus current.
result: The device exhibits multimode emission, current-dependent spectral reconfiguration, hysteresis in output power and spectrum, and mode switching at constant bias current.
conclusion: The observed behavior is attributed to interplay between scattered feedback and carrier-induced local refractive-index and temperature variations, offering a tunable platform for nonlinear laser applications.

title: Hopfion Superlattices In 3d Twisted Moir\'e Light Fields
authors: Yifan Zhang, Vasu Dev, Yijie Shen
abstract: ArXiv:2611.13476v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Moir\'e superlattices have recently been extended from electronic materials to photonic systems, enabling complex topological light fields such as skyrmion bags. However, these realizations remain confined to two dimensions. Here, we demonstrate 3D moir\'e superlattices formed by twisting multi-volume spatiotemporal optical lattices, giving rise to previously undiscovered 3D quasiparticle topologies, including hopfion bags, hopfion quasicrystals, and hopfion-hopfionium nested superlattices. By tailoring the interference polarization textures of the moir\'e spacetime lattices, we achieve controlled topological transitions among these states, and tailored topological numbers of hopfion bags. These spatiotemporal supertopologies offer a promising platform for high-capacity information encoding in higher dimensions.
tldr: The paper demonstrates 3D moiré superlattices formed by twisted spatiotemporal optical lattices, producing topological light quasiparticles such as hopfion bags, hopfion quasicrystals, and nested hopfion-hopfionium structures.
motivation: Moiré superlattices have been extended from electronic to photonic systems but so far remain confined to two dimensions; the authors aim to realize three-dimensional moiré superlattices and explore their topological quasiparticle states.
method: The authors twist multi-volume spatiotemporal optical lattices to create 3D moiré superlattices and tailor interference polarization textures to control topological transitions and topological numbers.
result: They demonstrate previously undiscovered 3D quasiparticle topologies, including hopfion bags, hopfion quasicrystals, and hopfion-hopfionium nested superlattices, with controlled topological transitions and tunable topological numbers.
conclusion: These spatiotemporal supertopologies provide a promising platform for high-capacity information encoding in higher dimensions, though the work is primarily in topological photonics rather than quantum information theory or related research directions.

title: A New Representation Of Effective Diffusion In Fluctuating Periodic Potentials Through Stochastic Duality
authors: Derek Frydel
abstract: ArXiv:2611.13526v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We revisit the classical problem of effective diffusion in fluctuating periodic force fields by combining homogenization with stochastic duality. We consider a specific class of fluctuations in which the internal state of the force field is independently redrawn from a fixed distribution at Poisson-distributed times. In the homogenization framework, the effective diffusion coefficient \(D_{\rm eff}\) is expressed in terms of a corrector function satisfying a backward Kolmogorov equation. For the redraw dynamics considered here, the equation governing the spatial derivative of the corrector can be reinterpreted as the stationary forward equation of a dual system obtained by reversing the force field, \(F\to-F\). This relation eliminates the corrector and yields a representation of \(D_{\rm eff}\) entirely in terms of stationary densities and probability currents of the physical and dual systems. We further introduce an auxiliary function \(Q(x)\) whose spatial variation is determined by the stationary current. When this current vanishes, \(Q(x)\) becomes independent of position and the effective diffusion coefficient reduces to the local relation \( D_{\rm eff}=L^2Q. \) This result generalizes the classical Lifson--Jackson relation to fluctuating periodic force fields. We verify the theory using analytical calculations, numerical solutions of the stationary equations, and direct simulations of the long-time particle displacement, including a driven system with nonzero stationary current.
tldr: The paper derives a new representation of the effective diffusion coefficient for classical Brownian particles in fluctuating periodic force fields using homogenization and stochastic duality.
motivation: Effective diffusion in fluctuating periodic potentials is a classical nonequilibrium statistical mechanics problem, and the authors seek a more transparent representation that avoids solving for the corrector function directly.
method: They combine homogenization theory with stochastic duality for force fields whose internal state is redrawn at Poisson times, reinterpreting the corrector equation as a stationary forward equation of a dual system with reversed force.
result: The effective diffusion coefficient is expressed solely through stationary densities and probability currents of the physical and dual systems, and a generalized Lifson-Jackson relation is obtained when the stationary current vanishes.
conclusion: The theory is verified analytically, numerically, and by direct simulations, including a driven system with nonzero stationary current, but it remains a purely classical stochastic-process result.

title: Quantum-Assisted Generative Anomaly Detection: A Dimension-Controlled Study Of Latent Refinement
authors: Thesath Wijayasiri, Omar Bacarreza, William Clements, Kar Wai Fok, Vrizlynn L. L. Thing
abstract: ArXiv:2611.13671v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Anomaly-based malware detectors learn what benign files look like and flag deviations. Generative approaches to this problem can make use of a "latent" or "prior" data representation, which is often chosen to be a Gaussian distribution. We ask whether the choice of prior distribution matters, and whether one produced by quantum hardware behaves differently from a classical one. Building on SAGEGAN, a style-based detector trained only on benign data, we compare three latent distributions: the original 512-dimensional Gaussian, a 48-dimensional Gaussian, and a 48-dimensional distribution sampled from an ORCA Computing PT-2 photonic quantum processor. We then refine each trained model's frozen representation using greedy and reinforcement-learning methods. Across ten random seeds, the quantum-derived model shows richer internal structure with better effective rank and latent similarity. It also benefits most from refinement. Though final detection accuracy is similar to that of the refined Gaussian latent, these findings show differences in latent geometry and refinement behavior between the trained configurations.
tldr: The paper compares Gaussian latent priors against a latent distribution sampled from a photonic quantum processor (ORCA PT-2) inside a style-based generative malware anomaly detector, then refines the frozen representations.
motivation: Anomaly-based malware detectors rely on a latent prior, usually Gaussian; the authors ask whether the choice of prior, and specifically a quantum-hardware-derived prior, changes the learned latent geometry and downstream detection.
method: Building on SAGEGAN trained only on benign data, three latent configurations (512-d Gaussian, 48-d Gaussian, 48-d quantum-sampled) are compared across ten random seeds, with each model's frozen representation subsequently refined using greedy and reinforcement-learning procedures.
result: The quantum-derived model exhibits richer internal structure, higher effective rank and better latent similarity, and benefits most from refinement, although final detection accuracy is comparable to the refined Gaussian baseline.
conclusion: Quantum-sampled priors may alter latent geometry and refinement dynamics of generative detectors, but no clear detection-accuracy advantage is demonstrated, leaving the practical benefit of quantum hardware in this pipeline an open question.

title: Closed-Form Gaussian Information Projection For Embedded Simplices And Simplicial Mixtures
authors: Ali Darijani, Emadedin Soufian, J\"urgen Beyerer
abstract: ArXiv:2611.13354v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Gaussian approximation of Dirichlet--Gaussian probability density functions on embedded simplices. We derive the unique information projection onto the family of nondegenerate ambient Gaussian probability density functions, obtaining closed-form expressions for the optimal Gaussian and the minimum divergence for arbitrary positive Dirichlet parameters. The minimum divergence depends only on the intrinsic simplex dimension and Dirichlet parameters, is invariant up to an affine isomorphism, independent of the ambient dimension, and independent of the normal covariance. Furthermore, by joint convexity of Kullback--Leibler divergence, we establish explicit intrinsic dimension-dependent sharp upper bounds for finite Gaussian Mixture with shared component weights. For uniform probability density functions, these bounds reduce to dimension-dependent constants. The results provide closed-form Gaussian Mixture constructions and rigorous approximation guarantees for probability density functions associated with embedded simplicial complexes. A numerical example on a circular curve illustrates the theoretical results and their connections to geometric Gaussian Mixture representations.
tldr: This paper derives closed-form Gaussian information projections for Dirichlet-Gaussian densities on embedded simplices and sharp KL-divergence bounds for Gaussian mixtures.
motivation: The authors aim to provide rigorous Gaussian approximation guarantees for probability densities associated with embedded simplicial complexes, motivated by geometric mixture representations.
method: They compute the unique information projection onto nondegenerate ambient Gaussian densities by minimizing Kullback-Leibler divergence and use joint convexity to bound finite Gaussian mixtures with shared weights.
result: Closed-form expressions are obtained for the optimal Gaussian and minimum divergence for arbitrary positive Dirichlet parameters, with bounds depending only on intrinsic simplex dimension and Dirichlet parameters.
conclusion: The work establishes dimension-dependent approximation guarantees and closed-form Gaussian mixture constructions, illustrated by a numerical example on a circular curve.

title: Kinematic Quantum Geometry
authors: Bernardo Barrera, Nishchhal Verma, Raquel Queiroz, Anatoli Polkovnikov, Anushya Chandran
abstract: ArXiv:2611.13089v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Kinematic quantum geometry describes fast degrees of freedom (DOFs) that adiabatically follow states parametrized by both the coordinates and the velocities of slow DOFs. It extends Born-Oppenheimer geometry, which depends on coordinates alone, introduces mixed Berry curvatures, and modifies the effective theory governing the slow DOFs. We test its predictions in two setups: spinful particles moving in magnetic textures, and Dirac electrons in graphene coupled to an LC circuit. In the first, kinematic quantum geometry produces a velocity-dependent effective mass tensor and generates a Lorentz-like force nonlinear in velocity that can arise even in coplanar textures. In the second, it renormalizes the circuit capacitance and generates a Hall current nonlinear in the electric field. For small velocities, it reproduces recent results for electronic dynamics in external electromagnetic fields and in pseudospin textures. However, the framework can remain valid at large velocities beyond the perturbative regime, provided the kinematic states are sufficiently slowly varying.
tldr: The paper introduces kinematic quantum geometry, extending Born-Oppenheimer geometry to fast degrees of freedom that adiabatically follow states depending on both slow coordinates and velocities.
motivation: Standard Born-Oppenheimer geometry depends only on slow coordinates, missing velocity-dependent geometric effects that can modify effective dynamics of slow degrees of freedom.
method: The authors develop a geometric framework with mixed Berry curvatures and test it in two settings: spinful particles in magnetic textures and Dirac electrons in graphene coupled to an LC circuit.
result: Kinematic geometry produces velocity-dependent effective mass tensors, nonlinear Lorentz-like forces, renormalized capacitance, and nonlinear Hall currents; it reduces to known perturbative results at small velocities.
conclusion: The framework extends quantum geometry beyond coordinate-only Born-Oppenheimer theory and may remain valid at large velocities when kinematic states vary slowly.

title: Universal Spectral Shapes Of Nonlinear Light Scattering From Laser-driven Dilute-gas Density Gratings
authors: Aleksei Zheltikov
abstract: ArXiv:2611.13341v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Operating within the framework of the collisionless Boltzmann equation, we identify universal spectral profiles inherent in stimulated and coherent light scattering from laser-driven dilute-gas density gratings and derive physically intuitive solutions for such spectral shapes, expressing them in a manifestly causal closed form that satisfies the Kramers - Kronig relations and fulfills the fluctuation - dissipation theorem. Benchmarking against gold-standard experiments on dilute-gas stimulated light scattering verifies a high descriptive and explanatory power of these solutions and demonstrates their ability to isolate universality motifs in nonlinear scattering spectra as the key to fully understanding the physics behind dilute-gas nonlinear light scattering. As one of important outcomes, such analysis reveals the physical content of the bandwidth of dilute-gas nonlinear scattering spectra as an expression and a quantifier of the phase-mixing time, i.e., the time required for free-streaming gas particles with a mean thermal velocity to traverse the distance equal to the spacing of the laser-driven density grating.
tldr: The paper derives universal spectral shapes for stimulated and coherent light scattering from laser-driven dilute-gas density gratings using the collisionless Boltzmann equation.
motivation: The author aims to identify universal spectral profiles in dilute-gas nonlinear light scattering and connect them to causal response functions and the fluctuation-dissipation theorem.
method: The analysis is based on the collisionless Boltzmann equation and derives closed-form causal spectral solutions satisfying Kramers-Kronig relations, benchmarked against experiments.
result: The solutions reproduce gold-standard dilute-gas stimulated light scattering experiments and reveal that the spectral bandwidth quantifies the phase-mixing time of free-streaming gas particles.
conclusion: The work provides an intuitive universal description of nonlinear light scattering spectra in dilute gases, but it is outside the target quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid-systems research directions.

title: Stress-controlled Avoided-crossing Evolution Of An Optical Microresonator Induced By Inter-fibre Side Coupling
authors: Misha Sumetsky Isha Sharma
abstract: ArXiv:2611.13722v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Analogies between quantum mechanics and photonics provide a powerful means of transferring concepts and phenomena between the two fields. Photonic analogues offer a distinctive advantage by allowing us to engineer and continuously vary parameters fixed by the microscopic structure of quantum systems, revealing richer behaviour. Building on these analogies, the recent demonstration of widely tunable microresonators formed by side coupling between optical fibres marked a significant advance in the development of reconfigurable resonant photonic systems. However, those methods offered no direct way to reach the centre of the avoided crossing, where the uncoupled fibre cutoff frequencies coincide and the modes hybridise most strongly. Here, we introduce an additional tuning degree of freedom by axially stretching a straight fibre coupled to a bent fibre. At essentially fixed coupling geometry, this lets us sweep the detuning between their uncoupled cutoff frequencies through zero. As the avoided crossing is approached, the induced microresonator's resonance band widens. Beyond the crossing, the band narrows and, strikingly, appears to "hang" below the stretched fibre's rising cutoff frequency. Our experimental results agree with coupled-mode theory and indicate the feasibility of 100 MHz-scale control of the straight-fibre cutoff frequency and the resonator spectral height over a tuning range of about 100 GHz, using a relative elongation of order [MATH].
tldr: The paper experimentally demonstrates stress-controlled tuning of an optical microresonator formed by side-coupled optical fibres through an avoided crossing using axial fibre stretching.
motivation: Photonic analogues of quantum mechanical avoided crossings allow tunable resonant systems, but previous side-coupled fibre microresonators could not access the centre of the avoided crossing where modes hybridise most strongly.
method: A straight fibre is axially stretched while coupled to a bent fibre, sweeping the detuning between their uncoupled cutoff frequencies through zero at essentially fixed coupling geometry; results are compared with coupled-mode theory.
result: Approaching the avoided crossing widens the induced microresonator resonance band, and beyond the crossing the band narrows and appears to hang below the stretched fibre's rising cutoff frequency, enabling ~100 MHz-scale cutoff control over ~100 GHz tuning range.
conclusion: Axial strain provides an additional tuning degree of freedom for fibre-based microresonators, enabling controlled access to the avoided-crossing regime and rich resonant behaviour consistent with coupled-mode theory.

title: Useful Work Can Increase Energy Use: Demand Elasticity And Proof Of Useful Work
authors: Or Sattath Isaiah Hull
abstract: ArXiv:2611.13131v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A serious criticism of Bitcoin's Proof-of-Work is its enormous electricity consumption. Proof-of-Useful-Work (PoUW), introduced by Ball, Rosen, Sabin, and Vasudevan (2017), in which mining performs useful computations, was suggested as an alternative to reduce electricity expenditure, with matrix multiplication (MatMul) as a recent concrete instantiation by Komargodski and Weinstein (2026). Perhaps surprisingly, we show that switching to PoUW may increase the total electricity consumption, echoing Jevons' paradox. Intuitively, the PoUW mechanism acts as a subsidy that lowers the effective price of the useful work. Recall that demand is elastic if a discount of x percent in the price leads to an increase of more than x percent in the quantity demanded. If demand is elastic, the resulting increase in quantity demanded leads to a net increase in total electricity consumption; if inelastic, total electricity consumption decreases. Even then, the electricity consumption due to PoUW never vanishes, since the mining subsidy is spent on useful work that would not have been produced without the subsidy. This result is proved in a simple model with electricity-only costs, no PoUW overhead, and an unchanged mining subsidy. The analysis extends to less restrictive settings with adjusted thresholds.
tldr: The paper argues that Proof-of-Useful-Work mining can increase total electricity consumption rather than reduce it, depending on demand elasticity for the useful work being subsidized.
motivation: Bitcoin's Proof-of-Work is criticized for huge electricity use, and Proof-of-Useful-Work has been proposed as a greener alternative; the authors question whether this actually lowers total energy expenditure.
method: The authors analyze a simple model with electricity-only costs, no PoUW overhead, and an unchanged mining subsidy, examining how the subsidy lowers the effective price of useful work and affects quantity demanded.
result: They show that if demand for the useful work is elastic, the induced increase in demand can raise total electricity consumption, echoing Jevons' paradox; if inelastic, consumption decreases but does not vanish.
conclusion: Switching to Proof-of-Useful-Work does not automatically reduce electricity use and may increase it, so energy-policy claims about PoUW require demand-elasticity considerations.

title: On Private Knowledge Retrieval And Private Inference For Secure Multi-agent Systems
authors: Maria Bras-Amor\'os Vicen\c{c} Torra
abstract: ArXiv:2611.13696v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-agent systems provide a convenient framework for the massive deployment of agents based on Large Language Models (LLMs). It provides a sound framework where agents can interact with existing software to perform actions in an autonomous way. Agentic AI is the new term to denote these AI-based autonomous systems. In real multi-agent systems, agents need to deal with malicious agents some of which can exploit security vulnerabilities to do harm. A memory poisoning attack is an example of exploiting a vulnerability to modify agents knowledge and, thus, affect its behavior. In an agent, there are different types of memory systems (semantic, episodic, and short-term) which have their own characteristics and for which different memory poisoning attacks may be developed. In this paper we focus on semantic memory, we discuss its attack, and mitigation strategies. We introduce private knowledge retrieval and private inference. We propose a signature system in the knowledge base to prevent from undesired manipulation. This should avoid memory poisoning attacks by introducing security by design in the construction of the semantic memory. In our architecture, an agent contains a local Prolog-like inference system (i.e., using Horn clauses to represent knowledge) which accesses an external knowledge base to get the required knowledge. This externally signed knowledge base is accessed privately. We provide different implementations in Python using different privacy levels including k-anonymity and information-theoretical privacy (IT-PIR).
tldr: The paper proposes privacy-preserving knowledge retrieval and inference for LLM-based multi-agent systems, using signed knowledge bases and cryptographic private information retrieval (including IT-PIR) to defend against memory poisoning attacks.
motivation: Autonomous LLM agents with semantic memory are vulnerable to memory poisoning and to leakage of queries against external knowledge bases, so security and privacy must be built into the memory architecture by design.
method: The authors describe semantic-memory poisoning attacks, propose a signature scheme over the knowledge base together with a local Prolog-like Horn-clause inference engine that accesses the signed external knowledge base privately, and give Python implementations offering several privacy levels including k-anonymity and information-theoretic PIR.
result: Multiple implementations at different privacy levels are provided, showing that signed knowledge combined with private retrieval can mitigate poisoning and query-leakage concerns in agentic settings.
conclusion: Design-level integration of signatures and private retrieval offers a practical route to more secure and private multi-agent LLM deployments, though the work is engineering-oriented rather than a quantum-information-theoretic contribution.

title: An Information-Theoretic Perspective On Regulatory T Cell Localization As An Il-2 Interference Filter
authors: Alexander Wietfeld, Kristina A. Ganzinger, Wolfgang Kellerer, Andrew W. Eckford
abstract: ArXiv:2611.14338v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Diffusible signals enable communication between immune cells but can also create interference between nearby activation sites. In lymph nodes, effector T cells (Teff) concentrate around antigen-presenting cells (APCs), release interleukin-2 (IL-2) following antigen recognition, and sense IL-2 through cell-surface receptors. Experiments show high-uptake regulatory T cells (Treg) clustered around IL-2-producing cells. However, it is unclear how strongly responses at neighboring activation sites are coupled through diffusible IL-2, and how this coupling is influenced by the spatial organization of Treg acting as IL-2 sinks. We interpret two neighboring sites as a molecular communication system and study the effect of clustering using a three-dimensional IL-2 field coupled to T cell population dynamics. Across a broad parameter sweep, clustering Treg produces a larger mean reduction in neighboring-site interference than adding dispersed Treg. Compared with no Treg, clustered Treg suppress interference while largely preserving the strong local response with corresponding consequences for population expansion and survival. Information-theoretic analysis shows improved discrimination between weak and strong local sources at short separation, whereas at larger separation clustering primarily reduces the remaining estimated neighboring-source information. These findings support a spatial-filtering role for Treg clustering in maintaining locally informative immune responses.
tldr: An information-theoretic model of how clustered regulatory T cells (Treg) act as IL-2 sinks that filter interference between neighboring T cell activation sites in lymph nodes.
motivation: Diffusible IL-2 enables communication between immune cells but also couples nearby activation sites; it is unclear how strongly such sites interfere and whether the observed spatial clustering of high-uptake Treg mitigates this.
method: Two neighboring activation sites are treated as a molecular communication system, modeled with a three-dimensional diffusive IL-2 field coupled to T cell population dynamics, swept over a broad parameter range and analyzed with information-theoretic discrimination measures.
result: Clustered Treg yield a larger mean reduction of neighboring-site interference than equal numbers of dispersed Treg, while preserving the strong local response; information-theoretic analysis shows improved discrimination of weak vs. strong local sources at short separation, with clustering mainly reducing estimated neighboring-source information at larger separations.
conclusion: Treg clustering functions as a spatial interference filter that helps maintain locally informative immune signaling, with consequences for T cell population expansion and survival.

title: Molecular Gas Optics Using Vibrational Population Density Refraction
authors: Daniel Matteo, Sergei Tochitsky, Chan Joshi
abstract: ArXiv:2611.13242v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Gas optics holds promise for development of advanced optical elements with 2-3 orders of magnitude higher damage threshold than any solid-state optics. Here, we demonstrate a new concept for refracting the laser beam using vibrationally excited molecules as gas optics instead of traditional control of thermodynamic gas temperature. The transient, vibrational population density grating is formed in a CO2 gas by interfering two mid-IR lasers to imprint spatial modulation in the linear refractive index (Delta n0 >=2x10-5) of the neutral gas via enhancement of the molecular polarizability. It is increased by pumping the asymmetric stretching mode of CO2 at optimal wavelengths to resonantly produce a highly nonequilibrium state that increases the effective vibrational mode temperature to greater than 2000 K in a room temperature gas. The measured beam steering efficiency of such a volume gas grating exceeds 90% that makes this approach a candidate for producing other large-aperture, high-throughput molecular optics elements, with expected damage thresholds 0.5-1 kJ/cm2, much-needed for future ultrahigh-power lasers.
tldr: The paper demonstrates a molecular gas-optics concept in which a vibrational population density grating in CO2 is used to steer laser beams via refractive-index modulation.
motivation: Solid-state optics suffer damage thresholds too low for ultrahigh-power lasers, motivating gas-based optical elements with much higher damage tolerance.
method: Two interfering mid-IR lasers resonantly pump the asymmetric stretching mode of CO2 to create a transient spatial modulation of vibrational excitation and thus of the linear refractive index.
result: The authors measure a refractive-index modulation Delta n0 >= 2x10^-5 and beam steering efficiency exceeding 90%, with estimated damage thresholds of 0.5-1 kJ/cm^2.
conclusion: Vibrationally excited molecular gases can serve as large-aperture, high-throughput optical elements for future ultrahigh-power laser systems.

title: The Wave Equation And Two-electron Atomic Wavefunctions
authors: John Lekner
abstract: ArXiv:2611.13320v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Axisymmetric solutions of the classical wave equation in three spatial dimensions are shown to be in one-to-one correspondence to functions which annihilate the two-electron kinetic energy operator expressed in coordinates relative to a fixed nucleus.
tldr: The paper establishes a mathematical correspondence between axisymmetric solutions of the classical three-dimensional wave equation and functions annihilating the two-electron kinetic energy operator in nucleus-relative coordinates.
motivation: The work aims to connect classical wave-equation solutions with the structure of two-electron atomic wavefunctions, likely to provide new mathematical representations or solution methods for atomic systems.
method: It uses analytical constructions relating axisymmetric wave-equation solutions to functions in the kernel of the two-electron kinetic energy operator expressed in relative coordinates.
result: A one-to-one correspondence is shown between these classical wave-equation solutions and functions annihilating the two-electron kinetic energy operator.
conclusion: The correspondence may offer a mathematical route for constructing or analyzing two-electron atomic wavefunctions, but it does not address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Fully GPU-accelerated Semistochastic Epstein-Nesbet Perturbation Theory
authors: Lizhong Fu, Honghui Shang, Jinlong Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.13522v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Second-order Epstein-Nesbet perturbation theory (EN-PT2) is an important tool for improving selected configuration interaction (SCI) energies, but the large external determinant space creates substantial memory and communication costs on GPU clusters. We develop a fully GPU-accelerated implementation of distributed semistochastic EN-PT2, fusing excitation generation, screening, and PT2 weighting in a single kernel traversal. Fixed-size random-phase CountSketch arrays limit memory use and replace large external determinant exchange with bounded collective summation. The implementation on one A100 completes EN-PT2 calculations 8.21-37.53 times faster than Arrow on 64 CPU cores at the same requested statistical standard error, and fixed-workload strong-scaling tests achieve 93.5% parallel efficiency on 16 GPUs across two nodes. Applications to an iron-oxo complex in a (60e, 187o) active space, iron-porphyrin references containing 200 million determinants per state, and neural-network quantum states establish the method's efficiency for perturbative corrections to large reference wave functions in the GPU era.
tldr: A fully GPU-accelerated distributed semistochastic second-order Epstein-Nesbet perturbation theory implementation for large-scale selected configuration interaction and neural-network quantum state calculations.
motivation: EN-PT2 improves SCI energies but the enormous external determinant space causes severe memory and communication bottlenecks on GPU clusters, limiting practical applicability to large active spaces.
method: The authors fuse excitation generation, screening, and PT2 weighting into a single GPU kernel traversal, use fixed-size random-phase CountSketch arrays to bound memory, and replace large external determinant exchanges with bounded collective summations.
result: On a single A100 the implementation is 8.21-37.53x faster than Arrow on 64 CPU cores at matched statistical error, with 93.5% parallel efficiency on 16 GPUs across two nodes, applied to an iron-oxo (60e,187o) active space and 200-million-determinant iron-porphyrin references.
conclusion: The method makes perturbative corrections to very large reference wave functions practical in the GPU era, but it is a quantum chemistry high-performance computing contribution with no quantum information or thermodynamic content.

title: Stochastic Evolution Of Interacting Directed Strings
authors: Deepak Dhar S. S. Manna
abstract: ArXiv:2611.13622v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the stochastic dynamics of a system of [MATH] polymer rings on an infinite cylinder with only excluded volume interaction, using simulations and also analytically. The strings can diffuse in the transverse direction by local Rouse-like moves where an up-kink changes to a down -kink, or vice versa. The motion is biased if the rates of flip are not equal. In the initial state, we start with a step initial condition: all the sites with a positive [MATH] coordinate are empty, and the sites with [MATH] are occupied with a uniform density. We study the scaling form of the density profile in the hydrodynamic limit. The scaling form is a function of [MATH] in the unbiased case, and a function of [MATH] in the biased case. In the unbiased case, in the steady state on a torus, the marginal probability distribution of the positions of the strings on a line with fixed [MATH]-coordinate is exactly same as that in the ground state of quantum-mechanical spin-less fermions on a line. The biased problem is equivalent to a growing surface in [MATH] dimension, which is expected to be in the Kardar-Parisi-Zhang universality class.
tldr: The paper studies stochastic dynamics of interacting directed polymer rings on a cylinder, analyzing density profiles, biased/unbiased scaling, and connections to fermionic ground states and KPZ growth.
motivation: The authors aim to understand hydrodynamic scaling and steady-state properties of interacting directed strings with excluded-volume interactions under local stochastic moves.
method: They use simulations and analytic arguments for Rouse-like kink-flip dynamics, including unbiased and biased rates, with step initial conditions on an infinite cylinder and torus.
result: The unbiased steady-state marginal distribution maps to the ground state of spinless fermions, while the biased problem maps to a growing surface expected in the KPZ universality class.
conclusion: The work characterizes scaling forms and nonequilibrium behavior of interacting directed strings, highlighting connections to free-fermion and KPZ physics.

title: Spectral-Domain Information Geometry Of Stationary Covariance Models: Gaussian And Elliptical Extensions
authors: Shu Yang, Dongying Li, Wenxian Yu
abstract: ArXiv:2611.13037v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper develops an information-geometric framework for stationary covariance structures. We begin with the infinite-dimensional setting, where stationary covariance structures can be characterized without finite-window boundary effects. By formulating the covariance structure as a bilinear form on a suitable class of test functions, we establish its spectral representation and show how finite-dimensional Toeplitz covariance matrices arise as restrictions to nested observation subspaces. For zero-mean proper complex Gaussian wide-sense stationary (WSS) processes, we show that the normalized finite-dimensional Fisher information converges to a spectral-domain metric. In logarithmic spectral coordinates, this metric becomes the standard [MATH] inner product, yielding an explicit Fisher--Rao distance that is also recovered as the asymptotic normalized affine-invariant Riemannian distance between Toeplitz covariance matrices. We then extend the framework to elliptical observation models by separating global covariance scale from shape. The shape Fisher information is orthogonal to radial nuisance directions and is characterized by a dimension- and radial-model-dependent coefficient. We derive a condition under which this coefficient converges to its Gaussian value as the observation dimension tends to infinity. The resulting limiting spectral-shape geometry is the centered [MATH] geometry of log-spectra and is invariant to positive rescaling. Numerical experiments illustrate the theoretical convergence results and the recovery of the Gaussian shape coefficient.
tldr: The paper develops an information-geometric framework for stationary covariance models, deriving spectral-domain Fisher information metrics for Gaussian WSS processes and extending the analysis to elliptical observation models.
motivation: The authors aim to characterize stationary covariance structures geometrically without finite-window boundary effects and to understand how finite-dimensional Fisher information converges to a spectral-domain metric.
method: They formulate covariance structures as bilinear forms on test functions, obtain spectral representations, show convergence of normalized finite-dimensional Fisher information to a spectral metric, and extend the framework to elliptical models by separating scale and shape.
result: In logarithmic spectral coordinates the metric becomes a standard inner product, yielding explicit Fisher-Rao and affine-invariant Riemannian distances; for elliptical models the shape Fisher information is orthogonal to radial nuisance directions and converges to the Gaussian coefficient under a derived condition.
conclusion: The limiting spectral-shape geometry is a centered geometry of log-spectra invariant to positive rescaling, and numerical experiments support the theoretical convergence results.

title: An Accelerated Power Method
authors: Rachael Tappenden
abstract: ArXiv:2611.13283v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An Accelerated Power Method (APM) for locating the dominant eigen-pair of a real, symmetric matrix is presented. The algorithm is motivated by Nesterov's Accelerated Gradient Method (AGM) and a connection between the APM and the AGM holds, that is analogous to the relationship between the Conjugate Gradient and Lanczos methods. Theoretical convergence analysis shows that the APM is guaranteed to recover the dominant eigen-pair of a normalized semi-definite matrix at a rate no worse than the Power Method. For normalized indefinite matrices, the APM will recover an extremal eigen-pair, but not necessarily the dominant one, and the rate can be worse than the vanilla PM, depending upon the choice of acceleration parameter. Computational practicalities are discussed, including parameter tuning, and numerical experiments are also presented.
tldr: A Nesterov-style accelerated power method for computing dominant eigenpairs of symmetric matrices, with convergence analysis and numerical experiments.
motivation: The power method is simple but slow; the authors seek to speed up dominant eigenpair computation by borrowing ideas from accelerated gradient methods, mirroring the Conjugate Gradient–Lanczos relationship.
method: An Accelerated Power Method (APM) is derived from Nesterov's accelerated gradient method, with convergence rates proved for normalized semi-definite and indefinite matrices, plus discussion of parameter tuning.
result: For semi-definite matrices APM converges no worse than the vanilla power method; for indefinite matrices it may converge to a non-dominant extremal eigenpair and can be slower depending on the acceleration parameter.
conclusion: APM offers a practical accelerated alternative to the power method, though guarantees are weaker for indefinite matrices and performance depends on tuning.

title: From Oscillations To Symmetry Breaking In A Two-dimensional Piecewise-smooth Dynamical System
authors: Oksana R. Satur
abstract: ArXiv:2611.13318v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a discrete-time dynamical model in which two players, each distributed over two positions, interact only at the positions of their maximal presence, with an intensity set by an external resource. The main idea is that the evolution of the maxima closes into a self-contained two-dimensional piecewise-smooth map that can be analysed exactly. We show that a single critical level of the resource separates two outcomes: below it, the players exchange leadership forever along a stable cycle; above it, the symmetry between them breaks, and an arbitrarily small initial advantage grows into a permanent winner--loser hierarchy. The local stability of these regimes is proved, and their global attractivity is supported by numerical experiments. At the critical level itself, all dominance is erased and both players end in equal division of the resource. Mathematically, the transition is a border-collision bifurcation shaped by this symmetry.
tldr: A two-dimensional piecewise-smooth map models two spatially distributed players whose interaction at their maximal-presence positions yields either perpetual leadership cycling or symmetry breaking into a permanent winner-loser hierarchy, controlled by a single critical resource level.
motivation: The authors aim to construct a minimal discrete-time model of competitive resource allocation between two distributed players that remains exactly analyzable while exhibiting a sharp transition between oscillatory coexistence and dominance.
method: The evolution of the players' maxima is reduced to a self-contained two-dimensional piecewise-smooth map, analyzed exactly via local stability analysis of the fixed points/cycles and by identifying the transition as a border-collision bifurcation; global attractivity is supplemented by numerical experiments.
result: Below a critical resource level the players exchange leadership indefinitely on a stable cycle; above it symmetry breaks and an arbitrarily small initial advantage amplifies into permanent dominance; at the critical level dominance vanishes and the resource is divided equally.
