conclusion: The choice of fractional order should be based on out-of-sample evidence rather than in-sample fit alone.

title: Proximal Point Algorithm For Interval Valued Optimization Problems With Application To Lasso Problem
authors: Anurag Jayswal, Sunidhi, Caihong Han
abstract: ArXiv:2611.13668v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we consider a class of unconstrained interval valued optimization problems and using a suitable scalarization technique, we formulate an associated scalarized optimization problem and establish the relationships between the optimal solution of the scalarized problem and the [MATH]-nondominated solution of the considered optimization problem. Based on this framework, we propose a proximal point algorithm and derive the global convergence of the sequence generated by the proposed algorithm along with the sublinear and linear rate of convergence for convex and strongly convex cases, respectively. Finally, we provide suitable numerical experiments along with comparative analysis with an existing method and applicability of the proposed algorithm on an interval valued lasso regression problem, highlighting its potential in machine learning models with uncertain data.
tldr: The paper develops a proximal point algorithm for unconstrained interval-valued optimization problems, with convergence-rate analysis and an application to interval-valued Lasso regression.
motivation: Interval-valued optimization handles optimization under data uncertainty, which the authors motivate by machine learning models with uncertain or imprecise data.
method: A scalarization technique reduces the interval-valued problem to a scalar one, relating its optima to [MATH]-nondominated solutions; a proximal point algorithm is then proposed and its global, sublinear (convex), and linear (strongly convex) convergence rates are derived.
result: Global convergence is proven with sublinear and linear rates for convex and strongly convex cases respectively, and numerical experiments against an existing method, including an interval-valued Lasso regression, show competitive performance.
conclusion: The framework offers a convergent proximal point method for interval-valued optimization with demonstrated applicability to uncertain-data regression tasks.

title: Enforcing Axioms For Ai Alignment Under Loss-Based Rules
authors: Sonja Kraiczy Alexandros Hollender
abstract: ArXiv:2611.13369v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many alignment methods, most notably reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF), train reward models by minimizing a loss on pairwise comparisons of model responses. Inspired by principle-guided methods such as Constitutional AI, we treat each principle as a voter that compares responses according to that principle, for example, preferring the more helpful or less toxic response. We represent these voters as linear directions in a fixed embedding space, a simplifying assumption motivated by the Linear Representation Hypothesis. In this linear social choice model, Ge et al. (2024) showed that an optimal linear reward model can violate Pareto optimality (PO): From the principles-as-voters lens, this means a response A can be less helpful and more toxic than B, yet still receive a higher reward. We ask whether richer reward models or changes to comparison data can recover PO within loss-based training. We show that PO can still fail for polynomials of any fixed degree and one-hidden-layer ReLU multilayer perceptrons (MLPs) of any fixed width [MATH] with suitable finite parameter bounds. We then recover PO for loss-based training of linear rewards under suitable assumptions in an idealized setting with uniform comparison directions and equal comparison lengths. These results motivate dataset design as an approach to recovering PO in constitutional-style alignment while retaining loss-based training.
tldr: The paper investigates whether Pareto optimality can be guaranteed in loss-based reward-model training for AI alignment, treating alignment principles as linear voters in an embedding space.
motivation: RLHF and constitutional-style alignment methods train reward models on pairwise comparisons, but optimal linear reward models can violate Pareto optimality, meaning a response that is less helpful and more toxic can still score higher.
method: The authors model principles as linear directions in a fixed embedding space (a linear social choice model) and analyze whether richer function classes—polynomials of fixed degree and one-hidden-layer ReLU MLPs of fixed width—or modified comparison data can recover Pareto optimality under loss-based training.
result: Pareto optimality can still fail for polynomials of any fixed degree and for one-hidden-layer ReLU MLPs of any fixed width under finite parameter bounds; however, PO is recoverable for linear rewards in an idealized setting with uniform comparison directions and equal comparison lengths.
conclusion: The findings motivate dataset design as a route to recovering Pareto optimality in constitutional-style alignment while retaining loss-based training.

title: 5g Cats: 5G-Based Cryptographic Authorization Against Trafficking Of Semiconductor Devices
authors: Sreevikram Rajaraman, Derek Ladd, Nicholas Heinrich-Barna, Srinivas Shakkottai, Jeyavijayan Rajendran
abstract: ArXiv:2611.13437v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Enforcing export controls on AI accelerators requires verifying where a chip operates after deployment. Round-trip time measurements can bound a chip's distance from a trusted landmark, but any jitter in honest replies forces the verifier to loosen its timeout, giving an attacker slack to relay traffic over fiber from a restricted region. Prior approaches either cross the untrusted host stack or rely on noisy power-line channels that inflate this slack. We present 5G CATS, a location certification system that pairs a co-packaged 5G radio, cryptographic engine, and hardware interlock on the GPU package with 5G Ultra-Reliable Low-Latency Communication (URLLC) base stations. Terminating the radio link inside the package removes the host software, PCIe fabric, and baseboard management controller from the verification path. We map an authenticated challenge-response protocol onto 5G's slot structure, replace permanent key erasure with short-lived execution leases, and specify a cross-check of the chip's reported serving cell against the carrier's own attachment records. In ns-3 and 5G-LENA simulations of an unloaded cell, our URLLC-based radio profile narrows the 99.9th percentile round-trip spread to 2.60 ms, more than ten times narrower than default 5G. A tracer rejects every round of a fiber relay from 300 km, against 2,000 km for default 5G. Against a 3,000 km attacker, a tracer stays safe at up to 1,410 km from the chip, against at most 619 km for PowerCATS's published model, while default 5G is never safe.
tldr: The paper proposes 5G CATS, a hardware-rooted location certification system using co-packaged 5G URLLC radios and cryptographic challenge-response to enforce export controls on semiconductor devices.
motivation: Verifying where AI accelerators operate after deployment is difficult because network jitter and untrusted host stacks give attackers slack to relay traffic from restricted regions.
method: The system integrates a 5G radio, cryptographic engine, and hardware interlock on the GPU package, maps an authenticated challenge-response protocol onto 5G slot timing, and cross-checks the reported serving cell against carrier attachment records.
result: Simulations show the URLLC profile reduces 99.9th-percentile round-trip spread to 2.60 ms, rejecting fiber relays from 300 km, and outperforming PowerCATS and default 5G under longer-distance attacks.
conclusion: Co-packaged 5G timing and cryptographic authorization can provide tighter location certification for semiconductor export control, though the work is classical hardware/network security rather than quantum information research.

title: Data-Efficient Unlearning-Based Backdoor Detection In Federated Learning
authors: Dowon Kim, Junhao Cai, Sung Il Choi, Dohun Kim, Juhyun Park, Chengjun Jin, Changhee Joo
abstract: ArXiv:2611.13491v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Detecting backdoor attacks in federated learning (FL) is challenging because malicious clients can manipulate the global model while preserving main-task performance. Static model-update statistics may therefore fail to clearly distinguish malicious from benign clients. Unlearning-based detectors instead probe client models through loss ascent on clean server data, but detection performance degrades with scarce proxy data. We propose Screening via Unlearning Response Analysis (SURA), a data-efficient detector. SURA reuses the same small clean proxy across multiple train-mode loss-ascent steps, strengthening client responses without additional clean data. For federated vision models with batch normalization (BN), repeated probing also changes BN running statistics and can confound endpoint measurements. SURA addresses this by restoring the shared pre-probe BN state only at readout while preserving the parameter changes induced by probing. This separates repeated probing from response measurement and removes BN drift and the interaction between parameter and BN-state changes from the readout. Across six backdoor attacks, SURA uses only 10 clean server images, outperforms methods under the same data budget, and approaches the robustness obtained with much larger proxy sets.
tldr: SURA is a data-efficient unlearning-based backdoor detector for federated learning that reuses a small clean proxy to strengthen client responses and corrects batch normalization drift during probing.
motivation: Backdoor detection in federated learning is difficult because malicious clients can preserve main-task performance, and existing unlearning-based detectors degrade when clean proxy data is scarce.
method: SURA repeatedly probes client models with train-mode loss ascent on the same small clean proxy, restores the shared pre-probe batch normalization state only at readout, and measures unlearning responses while avoiding BN-drift confounds.
result: Across six backdoor attacks, SURA uses only 10 clean server images, outperforms methods under the same data budget, and approaches robustness obtained with much larger proxy sets.
conclusion: The paper provides a practical, data-efficient backdoor detection method for federated vision models, but it is outside quantum information theory and related research directions.

title: Term: Target-Free Jailbreak Defense Via Entropy-Guided Residual Modulation
authors: Yunkai Dang, Wanyu Zhang, Meiyi Zhu, Qi Fan, Tianyu Ding, Wenbin Li
abstract: ArXiv:2611.13577v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have shown strong capabilities across diverse applications, making both safety and utility essential for reliable deployment. Jailbreak attacks use diverse forms of adversarial prompting to bypass alignment safeguards and induce LLMs to generate harmful responses. Some representation-based defenses regulate internal activations using predefined steering directions or learned safety regions. However, adapting intervention to each input without a predefined representational target while limiting over-refusal remains a challenge. In this paper, we propose Target-free Entropy-guided Residual Modulation (TERM), an inference-time defense that uses prompt-calibrated attention entropy deviations to guide adaptive modulation of the model's own residual updates. Attention patterns vary across prompts and decoding steps, making raw entropy values difficult to interpret as a consistent signal for intervention. We therefore calibrate attention entropy against each prompt's own prefill baseline to establish an input-specific reference for reducing unnecessary intervention on benign requests. Adaptive scale normalization and temporal accumulation then account for differences in deviation scale and persistence to determine intervention strength. The resulting signal controls bounded scaling of the model's own residual updates, without relying on a predefined safety direction. We compare our method with seven defenses on seven jailbreak attacks and two over-refusal benchmarks across Llama, Qwen, and Gemma models, including Qwen3 models from 0.6B to 32B. Results show our method improves jailbreak robustness while maintaining low over-refusal on benign safety-sensitive requests with modest inference overhead.
tldr: TERM is an inference-time jailbreak defense for large language models that modulates residual stream updates using prompt-calibrated attention entropy deviations, without requiring a predefined safety direction.
motivation: Representation-based defenses for LLM safety typically rely on predefined steering vectors or learned safety regions, which are rigid and can cause over-refusal on benign but safety-sensitive prompts; the authors aim for input-adaptive intervention without a fixed representational target.
method: The method computes attention entropy during prefill to establish a per-prompt baseline, then measures deviation during decoding, normalizing scale and accumulating over time to derive an intervention strength that bounds scaling of the model's own residual updates.
result: Across Llama, Qwen, and Gemma models (including Qwen3 0.6B–32B), TERM improved robustness against seven jailbreak attacks compared to seven baseline defenses while keeping over-refusal low on two benign safety benchmarks with modest inference overhead.
conclusion: Entropy-guided residual modulation offers a target-free, lightweight defense that balances jailbreak robustness and utility, though the work lies in LLM safety engineering rather than quantum information science.

title: Influence Of The Branching Geometry On Spion Propagation: Coupling Of Experiment And Simulation
authors: Daniel Fleischhauer, Luiz C. P. Wille, Stefan Lyer, Jens Kirchner, Dietmar Drummer
abstract: ArXiv:2611.13876v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Magnetic Drug Targeting (MDT) is an emerging therapeutic concept in cancer medicine, where superparamagnetic iron oxide nanoparticles (SPIONs) are used as carriers for medication. Their magnetic properties allow for the manipulation of particle transport within the vascular structure and thus targeted delivery to the tumor site. To develop effective concepts for particle steering and accumulation, a detailed understanding of the particle--flow interaction, especially at asymmetric vascular bifurcations, is needed. Based on hierarchical scaling laws, generalized bifurcation geometries with varying degrees of asymmetry were derived and additively manufactured. The particle distribution was investigated by in situ optical measurements under different flow conditions and magnetic field configurations and compared with Lagrangian particle and Volume of Fluid Simulations (VoFS). While the particle mass partition followed the hydraulic flow split in asymmetric bifurcations, density-driven stratification dominated in the symmetric bifurcation, where one daughter branch received only a minor fraction of the particle mass at low flow rates despite carrying half of the flow. The Lagrangian model reproduced the predominantly advective propagation, whereas only the VoFS approach captured the stratification-induced asymmetry. Magnetic actuation counteracted the stratification, reversed the passive branch preference and increased particle retention. From a molecular communication perspective, bifurcation geometry, collective volume effects and magnetic actuation thus jointly determine the received particle signal at vascular bifurcations.
tldr: The paper studies how vascular bifurcation geometry affects superparamagnetic iron oxide nanoparticle transport under flow and magnetic actuation, combining experiments and simulations.
motivation: Magnetic drug targeting requires understanding particle steering and accumulation at asymmetric vascular bifurcations to improve targeted delivery.
method: Generalized bifurcation geometries with varying asymmetry were additively manufactured and studied via in situ optical measurements, Lagrangian particle simulations, and Volume of Fluid simulations.
result: Particle mass partitioning followed hydraulic flow split in asymmetric bifurcations, while density-driven stratification dominated in symmetric bifurcations; magnetic actuation counteracted stratification and increased particle retention.
conclusion: Bifurcation geometry, collective volume effects, and magnetic actuation jointly determine particle signal at vascular bifurcations, with implications for molecular communication and targeted drug delivery.

title: Gradient Inversion Through Linear And Affine Subspace Constraints
authors: Athanasios P. Liavas Konstantinos Bouros
abstract: ArXiv:2611.13976v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Federated learning enables multiple clients to collaboratively train a machine-learning model without directly sharing their local datasets. However, as prior works have shown, the gradients exchanged during training may reveal sensitive information about client data. Most existing attacks usually optimize dummy inputs to match the true client gradients (Gradient Inversion Attacks), while some attempt to reconstruct them based on the observation that aggregate gradients from a fully connected (FC) layer are a linear combination of its inputs. In this work, we extend this observation by showing that aggregate gradients from an FC layer with the correct scaling are actually an affine combination of its inputs. We evaluate a gradient inversion attack that leverages either known linear-subspace information or its affine-subspace counterpart at each FC layer to improve reconstruction accuracy. Our results show that subspace-based methods can substantially improve reconstruction quality over the chosen baselines in certain settings. We further demonstrate that moderate overestimation of the batch size can generally improve or preserve reconstruction quality, even when the true batch size is unknown. We additionally examine reconstruction under gradient perturbations introduced by a differential privacy (DP) mechanism, providing insight into the effectiveness of the considered formulations under noisy conditions.
tldr: The paper shows that aggregate gradients of a fully connected layer form an affine combination of its inputs and exploits known linear or affine subspace constraints to improve gradient inversion attacks in federated learning.
motivation: Gradients exchanged during federated learning can leak sensitive client data, and existing gradient inversion attacks rely on optimizing dummy inputs rather than exploiting the algebraic structure of aggregate gradients.
method: The authors reformulate the FC-layer gradient relation as an affine combination with correct scaling, then evaluate gradient inversion attacks that impose either linear-subspace or affine-subspace constraints at each FC layer, including tests with overestimated batch sizes and differentially private gradient noise.
result: Subspace-based methods substantially improve reconstruction quality over baselines in certain settings, and moderate batch-size overestimation generally improves or preserves reconstruction quality even when the true batch size is unknown.
conclusion: Exploiting the affine/linear subspace structure of FC-layer gradients yields stronger privacy attacks, highlighting leakage risks in federated learning including under DP perturbations.

title: MammothDP: Private Boosted Decision Trees Ready For Trusted Hardware And Leakage-free Hyperparameters
authors: Moritz Kirschte, Thorsten Peinemann, Kari Kostiainen, Jan Wichelmann, Thomas Eisenbarth, Esfandiar Mohammadi
abstract: ArXiv:2611.14317v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Data spaces like the European Health Data Space (EHDS) require the protection of sensitive data in studies during the data's processing and the study's release alike. In this work, we investigate how to implement this mandate using established trusted execution environments (TEEs) and timing side-channel hardening to protect the processing even under a compromised server, and the state-of-the-art differential privacy (DP) notion to protect the release of studies on tabular data. This combined setup could seem to complete the picture, but in fact raises unexpected security challenges that we mitigate by introducing MammothDP: a significant milestone towards a holistic machine learning system based on the recent gradient boosted decision tree learner S-BDT that is provably DP if used within a privacy filter, timing side-channel hardened, and deployed on a TEE. To achieve a strong privacy-utility tradeoff, we introduce two novel components: an early stopping criterion that adaptively selects the number of trees without any privacy overhead, and an improved rollback protection that is no longer vulnerable under timing side-channel attacks.
tldr: MammothDP is a system for training differentially private gradient-boosted decision trees inside trusted execution environments with timing side-channel hardening and leak-resistant hyperparameter selection.
motivation: Regulations such as the European Health Data Space demand that sensitive tabular data be protected both during processing and upon release of study results, motivating a combination of TEEs and differential privacy.
method: The authors build on the S-BDT DP boosted-tree learner, deploy it on a TEE, harden it against timing side channels, and add an adaptive early-stopping rule that picks the number of trees without extra privacy budget plus improved rollback protection.
result: The resulting MammothDP system is provably differentially private under a privacy filter, timing-side-channel hardened, and deployable on trusted hardware, with improved privacy-utility tradeoff compared to prior approaches.
conclusion: The work provides a practical, security-hardened pipeline for private machine learning on sensitive tabular data, though its contributions are entirely classical and unrelated to quantum information science.

title: Species Sampling Priors Through Exact Augmentation
authors: Rams\'es H. Mena, Christos Merkatas, Theodoros Nicoleris, Carlos E. Rodr\'iguez
abstract: ArXiv:2611.13323v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Discrete random probability measures are central to Bayesian nonparametric mixture modeling and clustering. We show that every proper species sampling process (SSP) admits an exact two-stage finite representation of its sampling law. An almost surely finite index selects an initial set of atoms, and a draw is then made with explicitly reweighted probabilities. A decreasing visibility schedule determines both the reweighting and the index law. Averaging the finite conditional measures over this law recovers each realized SSP on every measurable set. Reversing this identity yields a novel and general method for constructing SSP priors from an index distribution and finite allocation probabilities, rather than specifying the infinite weights directly. We characterize compatibility between prescribed index probabilities, schedules and induced weights, and develop new SSP priors with full weak support using light-tailed, heavy-tailed and multimodal index distributions with suitable priors on their parameters. Within this framework, we couple marginal index laws with conditional weight distributions to construct SSP priors whose weights are invariant under size-biased permutation in their defining order. An example of such family is identified as the normalization of the sum of a gamma completely random measure and an independent compound-Poisson measure with gamma jumps, naturally leading to explicit partition and predictive laws. The joint distribution of the selected label and the finite index also gives exact simulation and recursive reweighting for SSPs. Total-variation bounds and numerical illustrations distinguish prior specification, exact averaging and fixed-level approximation.
tldr: The paper introduces an exact two-stage finite representation for species sampling processes and uses it to construct new Bayesian nonparametric priors.
motivation: Species sampling processes are central to Bayesian nonparametric mixture modeling and clustering, but priors are typically specified via infinite weights; the authors seek a more general and tractable construction.
method: They prove that every proper species sampling process admits an exact finite conditional representation involving an index distribution, a decreasing visibility schedule, and reweighted allocation probabilities, and they characterize compatibility conditions.
result: The framework yields new species sampling priors with full weak support, including families based on light-tailed, heavy-tailed, and multimodal index distributions, as well as exact simulation and total-variation bounds.
conclusion: The exact augmentation approach provides a flexible method for constructing and analyzing species sampling priors, with explicit partition and predictive laws.

title: Complete Decentralization Of Wave Equation Control On A Compact Domain
authors: Emily Jensen Addie Mccurdy
abstract: ArXiv:2611.13449v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A feedback control policy is completely decentralized if the actuation signal at each location in space can be computed based only on state information from that location. For systems equipped with large numbers of spatially distributed sensors and actuators, completely decentralized controllers are desirable since they can be implemented in a communication and computation efficient manner, but generally perform worse than centralized counterparts. However, through a case study of Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) design for wave dynamics on a compact spatial domain, we show that careful design of system parameters to satisfy certain conditions causes a decentralized control policy to perform as well as any centralized policy. We then propose a spatially filtered [MATH] norm to show that satisfying these conditions does not inherently degrade achievable closed-loop system performance, enabling simultaneous realization of both desirable performance and communication/computation efficiency via system-control co-design. Additional robustness analysis characterizes a range of system parameters such that the system interconnected with a decentralized controller maintains stability and near-optimal performance. Although our framework is derived for spatially continuous dynamics, we demonstrate that this theory can be leveraged to derive results for decentralization in finite-dimensional settings through a damped mass-spring example.
tldr: The paper studies completely decentralized LQR feedback control for wave dynamics on a compact domain and identifies conditions under which decentralized control matches centralized performance.
motivation: Large spatially distributed sensor-actuator systems benefit from communication- and computation-efficient decentralized controllers, but these usually perform worse than centralized policies.
method: Using a case study of LQR design for wave dynamics, the authors derive parameter conditions for optimal decentralized control and propose a spatially filtered norm for performance analysis, with robustness analysis and a damped mass-spring example.
result: Careful system-control co-design can make decentralized control perform as well as any centralized policy while preserving stability and near-optimal performance over a range of parameters.
conclusion: Decentralization need not inherently degrade closed-loop performance for wave equation control, enabling efficient implementation without sacrificing optimality under suitable conditions.

title: Two Nodally Bound-preserving And Mass-conservative Discontinuous Galerkin Methods For Reaction-diffusion Problems
authors: Zuodong Wang Jie Shen
abstract: ArXiv:2611.13588v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose and analyze two high-order discontinuous Galerkin methods that preserve prescribed nodal bounds and total mass for reaction-diffusion problems with anisotropic and heterogeneous diffusion. Both methods combine a weighted interior-penalty prediction step with a convex correction in either the dG energy or the [MATH] metric. We construct a pointwise bound-preserving and cellwise mass-preserving comparison function with optimal local approximation properties. This construction yields optimal dG-energy error estimates for the energy correction and, under a dual regularity assumption, optimal [MATH] and dG-energy error estimates for the [MATH] correction on quasi-uniform meshes. We further establish a general a posteriori estimate that combines a predictor estimator with the computable correction norm. The resulting estimators are globally reliable and efficient up to data oscillation, with parameter-dependent efficiency constants. Numerical experiments compare the two corrections and illustrate their use in adaptive computations.
tldr: The paper develops two high-order discontinuous Galerkin methods for reaction-diffusion problems that preserve nodal bounds and total mass.
motivation: Reaction-diffusion equations with anisotropic and heterogeneous diffusion require numerical schemes that respect physical bounds and conservation properties.
method: The authors combine weighted interior-penalty prediction with convex correction in either the dG energy or L2 metric, and construct a comparison function with optimal local approximation properties.
result: They derive optimal dG-energy error estimates for the energy correction and, under dual regularity, optimal L2 and dG-energy estimates for the L2 correction, plus reliable and efficient a posteriori estimators.
conclusion: Numerical experiments compare the corrections and demonstrate their use in adaptive computations.

title: Wave-Domain Semantic Isac: Holographic Surfaces As Analog Semantic Encoders For Integrated Tn-ntn
authors: Shadi Danesh, Pooria Salami, Hesaam Zaravashan, Abdulkadir K\"ose, Ayhan Akbas, Chuan Heng Foh, Mohsen Khalily
abstract: ArXiv:2611.14094v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Semantic communication, near-field operation, and integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) are often considered separately in terrestrial and non-terrestrial networks (TN--NTN). We show how a large electromagnetic aperture can connect them. {Nonlocal metasurfaces and holographic apertures act on the spatial spectrum of an incident field and can execute linear projections, which form an early stage of semantic feature extraction, directly in the wave domain before digitisation, thereby reducing the corresponding digital processing burden.} Near-field focusing also provides position-dependent sensing features, allowing the aperture to serve as an analog semantic-ISAC front end on resource-constrained aerial and satellite platforms. We describe the underlying physics, the co-design of constrained analog projections with lightweight digital decoders, and a case study in which a data-adaptive projection outperforms a fully digital baseline in the simulated energy-limited regime while transmitting four times fewer coefficients and using 11.4 times fewer decoder MACs. Finally, we identify relevant 3GPP, ITU-R, and ETSI activities and the remaining standardisation gaps.
tldr: The paper proposes using nonlocal metasurfaces and holographic apertures as analog semantic encoders that perform linear projections in the wave domain for integrated sensing and communication in terrestrial and non-terrestrial networks.
motivation: Semantic communication, near-field operation, and ISAC are typically treated separately in TN-NTN settings, and resource-constrained aerial/satellite platforms need to reduce digital processing burden.
method: The authors describe the underlying wave-domain physics of large electromagnetic apertures acting on the spatial spectrum, co-design constrained analog projections with lightweight digital decoders, and run a simulated energy-limited case study against a fully digital baseline.
result: The data-adaptive analog projection outperforms the fully digital baseline in the simulated energy-limited regime while transmitting four times fewer coefficients and using 11.4 times fewer decoder MACs.
conclusion: Large-aperture holographic surfaces can serve as analog semantic-ISAC front ends, and the authors identify relevant 3GPP/ITU-R/ETSI activities and remaining standardization gaps.

title: Gard: Gradient-Guided Adversarial Representation Defense Against Backdoors In Multimodal Contrastive Learning Models
authors: Yuhong Wang, Yujun Cai, Lei Feng, Songze Li
abstract: ArXiv:2611.14143v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multimodal contrastive learning models such as CLIP are vulnerable to backdoor attacks with diverse trigger structures, ranging from localized patches to globally distributed perturbations, with recent attacks increasingly optimizing these triggers in the representation space. Existing post-hoc defenses based on clean fine-tuning may leave backdoors active, while trigger-inversion methods depend on accurately estimating the attack target and trigger. We observe that backdoored encoders exhibit structure-dependent representation sensitivity: global perturbations preferentially expose distributed backdoors, whereas local patch perturbations are more effective for localized backdoors. Based on this observation, we propose Gradient-Guided Adversarial Representation Defense (GARD), a target- and trigger-agnostic post-hoc defense. GARD optimizes complementary global and local adversarial probes to maximally displace clean-image representations, and then realigns the perturbed representations with detached clean anchors while preserving image-text alignment. The resulting model requires no additional computation at inference time. Across six visual backdoor attacks and two CLIP visual backbones, GARD reduces the attack success rate below 1% in all 12 evaluated attack-backbone combinations while maintaining competitive clean accuracy. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of adversarial representation probing for repairing backdoored multimodal contrastive encoders.
tldr: GARD is a post-hoc, target- and trigger-agnostic defense that repairs backdoored CLIP-style multimodal contrastive encoders using gradient-guided global and local adversarial representation probing.
motivation: Multimodal contrastive models such as CLIP are vulnerable to backdoor attacks with diverse trigger structures, and existing clean fine-tuning or trigger-inversion defenses are insufficient or depend on accurate estimation of the attack target and trigger.
method: The authors exploit structure-dependent representation sensitivity to design complementary global and local adversarial probes that maximally displace clean-image representations, then realign perturbed representations with detached clean anchors while preserving image-text alignment, requiring no extra inference cost.
result: Across six visual backdoor attacks and two CLIP visual backbones, GARD reduces attack success rate below 1% in all 12 attack-backbone combinations while maintaining competitive clean accuracy.
conclusion: Adversarial representation probing is an effective, trigger-agnostic strategy for repairing backdoored multimodal contrastive encoders without inference overhead.

title: A NURBS-enhanced High-order Finite-volume Method For Compressible Laminar Boundary Layers On Curved Domains With Hybrid Meshes
authors: Yisu Li, Xucheng Meng, Guanghui Hu
abstract: ArXiv:2611.13463v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-fidelity simulation of compressible laminar boundary layers on curved domains requires physical wall boundary treatment and geometric representation compatible with high-order reconstruction, since viscous shear stresses and conductive heat fluxes are concentrated in a thin near-wall region. Conventional high-order methods often suffer from loss of accuracy near curved walls or require complicated wall treatments. To address these issues, in this paper, we develop a NURBS-enhanced [MATH]-exact finite-volume method for the steady compressible Navier--Stokes equations on hybrid meshes. To incorporate physical wall conditions into the high-order discretization, we develop a wall boundary treatment that employs sequential reconstruction without requiring the reconstruction variables to coincide with those used to prescribe the boundary conditions. The NURBS-based boundary representation is used to obtain a high-order accurate description of curved boundaries, and the diffusive generalized Riemann problem (dGRP) viscous flux is employed to enhance numerical robustness. A variety of numerical examples are provided to demonstrate the high-order accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed method.
tldr: This paper develops a NURBS-enhanced high-order finite-volume method for simulating compressible laminar boundary layers on curved domains using hybrid meshes.
motivation: High-fidelity simulation of compressible laminar boundary layers on curved walls is challenging because conventional high-order methods lose accuracy near curved boundaries or require complicated wall treatments, especially where viscous stresses and heat fluxes concentrate.
method: The authors propose an [MATH]-exact finite-volume scheme for the steady compressible Navier-Stokes equations on hybrid meshes, combining a sequential-reconstruction wall boundary treatment, NURBS-based boundary representation for curved geometries, and a diffusive generalized Riemann problem (dGRP) viscous flux for robustness.
result: A range of numerical examples demonstrate high-order accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed method on curved domains with hybrid meshes.
conclusion: The NURBS-enhanced approach provides an accurate and robust framework for high-order simulation of compressible laminar boundary layers, avoiding accuracy loss at curved walls without complicated boundary treatments.

title: Geometry-Dependent Dimension Jumps In Planar $C^r$ Splines At Degree $2r+1$
authors: Yi Zheng, Jiansong Deng, Xinyu Wu
abstract: ArXiv:2611.12996v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study geometric dependence of the dimensions of planar spline spaces [MATH] through families with a single moving interior vertex and determine their dimensions throughout the admissible parameter domains. For [MATH], we extend the Wu--Deng one-parameter classification to the interior of the central quadrilateral. The dimension increases by one at exactly two isolated points, one due to a local direction-count change and the other to a global compatibility defect. For [MATH], subdividing one triangle of the Yuan--Stillman configuration gives a twelve-triangle family with fixed local direction counts; its dimension increases by one precisely on an open line segment. For every [MATH], we construct a family with [MATH] triangles and fixed local direction counts, proving geometric dependence at degree [MATH]. The moving vertex lies in an open triangle, and the dimension exceeds Schumaker's lower bound by one exactly on its symmetry axis. The lower collinear vertices may have arbitrary strictly ordered heights. The low-order proofs use exact cofactor elimination. For higher orders, weighted interpolation and block elimination bound the global defect by one, and explicit extension and obstruction arguments determine the exceptional set.
tldr: The paper determines the dimension of planar C^r spline spaces as a function of the geometry of a configuration with one moving interior vertex, showing dimension jumps at isolated points and segments at various degrees.
motivation: The dimension of planar spline spaces depends subtly on the geometry of the underlying triangulation, and existing classifications (e.g., Wu–Deng, Yuan–Stillman) covered only restricted cases; the authors aim to characterize this geometric dependence across admissible parameter domains and degrees.
method: Families of triangulations with a single moving interior vertex and fixed local direction counts are constructed; dimensions are computed via exact cofactor elimination at low orders, and via weighted interpolation and block elimination to bound the global defect at higher orders, with explicit extension and obstruction arguments identifying the exceptional sets.
result: For r=2 the dimension increases by one at exactly two isolated points (one from a local direction-count change, one from a global compatibility defect); for r=3 subdivision of the Yuan–Stillman configuration yields a twelve-triangle family whose dimension jumps on an open line segment; for every r a family with 2r+1 triangles exhibits geometric dependence, exceeding Schumaker's lower bound by one exactly on a symmetry axis.
conclusion: Geometric dependence of spline space dimension is proven at degree 2r+1 for all r, extending and unifying earlier low-degree classifications and showing that dimension jumps can occur on isolated points, segments, or symmetry axes depending on the configuration.

title: Adaptive Local Fr\'echet Regression With Polyspherical Predictors
authors: Chang Jun Im
abstract: ArXiv:2611.13240v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study local Fr\'echet regression for responses taking values in a metric space and predictors on a product of spheres of possibly different dimensions. We propose local constant and local linear estimators with factor-specific bandwidths and establish uniform convergence rates. We select sphere factors by comparing cross-fitted prediction risks for the full and leave-one-factor-out models. The procedure consistently recovers the active factor set, and the selected local constant and local linear estimators attain the same uniform convergence rates as if the active factor set were known. For univariate Wasserstein responses supported on a common compact interval, the uniform rate holds without an entropy condition on the response space. Simulations with scalar and spherical responses and analyses of vessel speeds and drifter speed distributions illustrate the methods.
tldr: The paper develops adaptive local Fréchet regression methods for metric-space responses with predictors on products of spheres.
motivation: It addresses regression when responses lie in a general metric space and predictors are polyspherical, requiring factor-specific bandwidths and variable selection over sphere factors.
method: The author proposes local constant and local linear Fréchet estimators with factor-specific bandwidths and selects active sphere factors by comparing cross-fitted prediction risks for full and leave-one-factor-out models.
result: The procedure consistently recovers the active factor set, and the selected estimators achieve uniform convergence rates matching the oracle case; for univariate Wasserstein responses on a common compact interval, the uniform rate holds without an entropy condition.
conclusion: The work provides adaptive estimation and factor selection for Fréchet regression with polyspherical predictors, illustrated by simulations and analyses of vessel speeds and drifter speed distributions.

title: Weak Convergence Orders For A Fully Discrete Approximation Of Semilinear Stochastic PDEs Driven By Multiplicative Gaussian And Poisson Noise
authors: Chuchu Chen, Jialin Hong, Ziyi Lei, Xu Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.13467v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates the weak convergence of a fully discrete approximation for a class of semilinear stochastic partial differential equations (SPDEs) driven by multiplicative Gaussian and Poisson noise. The scheme combines a spectral Galerkin discretization in space with an exponential Euler discretization in time. Compared with single-noise settings, the simultaneous presence of continuous and jump perturbations introduces additional challenges arising from discontinuous trajectories, nonlocal jump operators, and their interaction with state-dependent multiplicative coefficients. To overcome these difficulties, we establish the exponential integrability of the numerical solution processes and refined moment estimates in negative Sobolev norms for the associated first- and second-order variational processes. Combining these estimates with a discrete-time approximation argument and Wiener--Poisson Malliavin calculus, we derive regularity estimates for the solutions of the Kolmogorov equations associated with the spatial Galerkin approximations. Based on these estimates, we obtain the temporal and spatial weak convergence orders arbitrarily close to one with respect to discretization parameters [MATH] and [MATH], respectively. To the best of our knowledge, this provides the first weak convergence result for a fully discrete approximation of semilinear SPDEs with simultaneous multiplicative Gaussian and Poisson noise.
tldr: This paper derives weak convergence orders for a fully discrete spectral Galerkin / exponential Euler scheme approximating semilinear stochastic PDEs driven simultaneously by multiplicative Gaussian and Poisson noise.
motivation: Weak convergence theory for SPDEs with a single noise type is well developed, but the combination of continuous Gaussian and discontinuous jump (Poisson) perturbations with state-dependent multiplicative coefficients poses new analytical difficulties that had not been treated for fully discrete schemes.
method: The authors combine spectral Galerkin spatial discretization with exponential Euler time stepping, and prove exponential integrability plus refined negative-Sobolev-norm moment estimates for first- and second-order variational processes, using discrete-time approximation and Wiener-Poisson Malliavin calculus to obtain regularity of Kolmogorov equation solutions.
result: They obtain temporal and spatial weak convergence orders arbitrarily close to one in the discretization parameters, claimed to be the first such fully discrete weak convergence result for semilinear SPDEs with simultaneous multiplicative Gaussian and Poisson noise.
conclusion: The work extends numerical weak-convergence analysis to jump-diffusion SPDEs, but remains a purely stochastic-numerics contribution with no connection to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum platforms.

title: A Variable-metric Inexact Progressive Hedging Algorithm With A Lagged Stopping Criterion For Multistage Stochastic Variational Inequalities
authors: Min Zhang, Lei Yang, Jie Sun
abstract: ArXiv:2611.13547v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The progressive hedging algorithm (PHA) solves multistage stochastic variational inequalities (SVIs) by independently solving regularized scenario subproblems and enforcing nonanticipativity through primal-dual updates. Since these subproblems are often solved iteratively, practical implementations need stopping criteria that control errors while preserving convergence. We propose iVMPHA-Lag, a variable-metric inexact PHA with a lagged stopping criterion for monotone SVIs. The method allows scenario block metrics to vary across outer iterations while remaining compatible with nonanticipativity. For each scenario, an error budget combines a positive fraction of the previous budget with a progress measure from the preceding outer iteration. This gives a stopping tolerance fixed before the inner iterations begin, so each scenario can check its criterion independently without a prescribed summable tolerance sequence. With positive initial budgets and a positive inexactness parameter, we prove finite inner termination provided the inner solver produces valid approximations whose residual and enlargement errors tend to zero. Under suitable conditions, we establish global convergence of the primal-dual iterates and local [MATH]-linear convergence under metric subregularity at the limit point. Numerical experiments on synthetic strongly monotone box-constrained SVIs show that iVMPHA-Lag with adaptive metrics uses fewer scenario evaluations and less time on average than exact PHA and the competing inexact methods among the tested configurations in all four baseline regimes. Its average time advantage over the competing inexact methods persists across the tested problem sizes. Further comparisons show that metric adaptation improves efficiency over the fixed scalar configuration, while lagged stopping and positive budget retention reduce inner computational work.
tldr: The paper proposes iVMPHA-Lag, a variable-metric inexact progressive hedging algorithm with a lagged stopping criterion for solving multistage stochastic variational inequalities.
motivation: Practical implementations of progressive hedging need stopping criteria for inexactly solved scenario subproblems that control error while preserving convergence, without requiring prescribed summable tolerance sequences.
method: The authors introduce scenario block metrics that vary across outer iterations and define per-scenario error budgets combining a fraction of the previous budget with a progress measure from the previous outer iteration, then prove finite inner termination, global convergence, and local linear convergence under metric subregularity.
result: Numerical experiments on synthetic strongly monotone box-constrained SVIs show fewer scenario evaluations and lower average runtime than exact PHA and competing inexact methods across four baseline regimes and tested problem sizes.
conclusion: Adaptive metrics, lagged stopping, and positive budget retention together improve the efficiency of inexact progressive hedging for multistage stochastic variational inequalities.

title: The Fermat--Torricelli Problem Under Isosceles Orthogonality-type Conditions
authors: Qi Liu Zhiyao Fang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.13648v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The location problem studied by Weber leads to the Fermat--Torricelli problem of minimizing sums of distances. Ben\'{i}tez, Fern\'{a}ndez and Soriano proved that a real normed space of dimension at least three is an inner-product space if and only if every triple of points has a Fermat--Torricelli median in its convex hull. Pakhrou showed that it suffices to test equilateral triangles. We establish a characterization using triangles [MATH] satisfying \[ \|x+y\|=\lambda\|x-y\|,\qquad \forall\,\lambda>2/3, \] with the parameter fixed in each characterization. The case of parameter one gives an isosceles orthogonality criterion. The proof combines radial rescaling with the transfer of planar minimality to the ambient space, without completeness or regularity assumptions on the norm.
tldr: This paper characterizes inner-product spaces via Fermat--Torricelli medians under isosceles-orthogonality-type triangle conditions.
motivation: The Fermat--Torricelli problem and its normed-space characterizations connect geometric minimization with the structure of normed spaces, extending prior results that use triples or equilateral triangles.
method: The authors use triangles satisfying a parameterized norm identity, combining radial rescaling with transfer of planar minimality to the ambient space, without completeness or regularity assumptions.
result: They obtain a characterization of inner-product spaces using such triangles, with the parameter-one case recovering an isosceles orthogonality criterion.
conclusion: The work provides a new geometric characterization of inner-product spaces within normed spaces, but it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Unstable Entropy And Volume Growth For Partially Hyperbolic Diffeomorphisms
authors: Yuntao Zang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.13682v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be a [MATH] diffeomorphism on a compact manifold [MATH] admitting a partially hyperbolic splitting [MATH] where [MATH] is uniformly expanding. We establish a lower bound for the unstable topological entropy (w.r.t. [MATH]): $[MATH][MATH]E^{cs}[MATH]\limsup$ is in fact a limit.
tldr: The paper proves a lower bound for the unstable topological entropy of partially hyperbolic diffeomorphisms with uniformly expanding center-unstable direction, and shows a limsup expression is actually a limit, linking unstable entropy to volume growth.
motivation: Topological entropy of partially hyperbolic systems is difficult to compute; relating unstable entropy to geometric quantities like volume growth gives computable invariants and clarifies the entropy structure along expanding directions.
method: Pure mathematical techniques from smooth ergodic theory and partially hyperbolic dynamics: unstable manifolds, topological entropy defined with respect to the center-stable direction, and comparison with volume growth of unstable leaves under iterates of the diffeomorphism.
result: A lower bound on the unstable topological entropy is established, and the corresponding limsup quantity is proven to converge to a genuine limit.
conclusion: The work refines the entropy theory of partially hyperbolic diffeomorphisms, providing a volume-growth-based estimate and regularity (existence of a limit) for unstable entropy.

title: Communication-Learning Co-Design For Pinching-Antenna-Assisted Federated Learning In Heterogeneous Wireless Networks
authors: Shuai Wang, Wenxuan Sun, Mingjie Shao, Wantao Jiang, Yanqing Xu, Lingxiang Li, Zhi Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2611.13987v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Wireless federated learning (FL) suffers from two coupled bottlenecks: statistical heterogeneity across clients and communication-constrained model synchronization over unreliable wireless links. Instead of focusing on algorithmic design and/or wireless resource optimization, this paper provides a systematic study of pinching antenna (PA)-empowered FL for heterogeneous wireless networks and develops a unified communication-and-learning framework. Specifically, we integrate a segmented waveguide-enabled pinching antenna (SWAN) architecture with a heterogeneity-robust FL algorithm based on client variance reduction and dual quantization, so as to jointly mitigate communication bottlenecks and client drift. On this basis, we further develop a two-stage SWAN-assisted downlink protocol and formulate fairness-oriented uplink optimization problems for PA positioning, bandwidth allocation, and quantization design. Efficient solution frameworks are then derived for the resulting downlink and uplink optimization problems. Experimental results show the superiority of the proposed design in convergence speed and final accuracy under non-independent and identically distributed data and communication bottlenecks.
tldr: This paper co-designs a segmented waveguide-enabled pinching antenna architecture with a heterogeneity-robust federated learning algorithm to mitigate client drift and communication bottlenecks in wireless networks.
motivation: Wireless federated learning is limited by statistical heterogeneity across clients and communication-constrained model synchronization over unreliable links, motivating a joint communication-and-learning design.
method: The authors integrate a pinching-antenna (SWAN) architecture with a variance-reduced, dual-quantized FL algorithm, develop a two-stage downlink protocol, and formulate fairness-oriented uplink optimization problems for antenna positioning, bandwidth allocation, and quantization.
result: Experiments show improved convergence speed and final accuracy under non-IID data and communication bottlenecks compared with baselines.
conclusion: Pinching-antenna-assisted communication-learning co-design offers a viable path to more efficient and fair wireless federated learning in heterogeneous networks.

title: Isolation Is Not Confidentiality: Security Boundaries Of Geometric Access Control In Rag
authors: Steve Nouyep, Maxime Puys, S\'ebastien Salva
abstract: ArXiv:2611.14061v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems increasingly rely on vector databases containing documents governed by different access-control policies. Recent search-preserving geometric approaches enforce such access control by structuring the embedding space so that transformed embeddings, which we call protected representations, remain retrievable without exposing information across policy boundaries. We provide a unified security analysis of this paradigm, covering policy isolation, representation confidentiality, query forgery resistance, and policy-membership hiding. We consider both a curious cloud service provider observing the protected representations stored in the vector database and a curious user holding aligned pairs of original embeddings and protected representations. Evaluating the available implementations of the works proposing these geometric transformation mechanisms across three encoders, we find that geometric transformations preserve retrieval utility and provide strong policy isolation, but do not provide the other security properties. A curious user can recover the original embeddings from a few hundred pairs and forge policy-compatible queries at a higher cost that grows with encoder dimension for secret per-policy transformations. Moreover, policy-dependent geometry can leak policy membership even when unauthorized retrieval is prevented. These results show that policy isolation, confidentiality, forgery resistance, and membership hiding are distinct security objectives.
tldr: The paper analyzes security boundaries of geometric access-control transformations in RAG vector databases, showing that policy isolation does not imply representation confidentiality, query forgery resistance, or policy-membership hiding.
motivation: RAG systems increasingly store documents under heterogeneous access policies, and geometric embedding transformations have been proposed to preserve retrieval while enforcing access control. The authors aim to clarify which security properties these mechanisms actually provide.
method: The authors give a unified security analysis of geometric access-control approaches, considering a curious cloud provider and a curious user with aligned original/protected embedding pairs. They evaluate available implementations across three encoders against policy isolation, representation confidentiality, query forgery resistance, and policy-membership hiding.
result: Geometric transformations preserve retrieval utility and provide strong policy isolation, but fail to provide the other security properties: a curious user can recover original embeddings from a few hundred pairs, forge policy-compatible queries, and policy-dependent geometry can leak policy membership.
conclusion: Policy isolation, confidentiality, forgery resistance, and membership hiding are distinct security objectives. Geometric access control in RAG should not be treated as providing confidentiality or query-forgery resistance without additional mechanisms.

title: Complexity Of Deciding Existence Of Maltsev Polymorphisms Of Finite Relational Structures
authors: Ali Syed Dejan Delic
abstract: ArXiv:2611.14379v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article, we show that the problem of deciding whether a finite relational structure [MATH] admits a Maltsev polymorphism is a computational problem, which can be solved in polynomial time. We provide a proof of this result by reducing the problem to deciding whether a binary relational structure, associated with [MATH] admits such a polymorphism. In our construction of such an algorithm, we make an extensive use of a property of binary relations, which is implied by the existence of a Maltsev polymorphism, the so-called rectangularity property.
tldr: The paper proves that deciding whether a finite relational structure admits a Maltsev polymorphism can be done in polynomial time, via a reduction to binary relational structures exploiting the rectangularity property.
motivation: Maltsev polymorphisms characterize tractable constraint satisfaction problems, so determining their existence is a central question in the complexity classification of CSPs and universal algebra.
method: The authors reduce the general problem to the corresponding decision problem for an associated binary relational structure and design a polynomial-time algorithm that repeatedly exploits rectangularity, a property implied by the presence of a Maltsev polymorphism.
result: A polynomial-time algorithm is obtained for deciding the existence of a Maltsev polymorphism in finite relational structures, matching the reduced binary case.
conclusion: The work settles the computational complexity of a basic algebraic tractability test for CSPs, with algorithmic implications for the algebraic approach to constraint satisfaction.

title: Overcoming Dynamic Range Limitations In Computational Hyperspectral Imaging
authors: Qianqian Yu, Jinhang Lin, Zhihai Yao, Shuo Wang, Chaofan Weng, Xiang Hao
abstract: ArXiv:2611.13663v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Computational hyperspectral imaging offers compact spectral sensing, yet imaging high-dynamic-range (HDR) scenes remains challenging. Accurate spectral reconstruction requires encoded measurements to remain within the calibrated linear-response range and above the noise floor. Due to unequal spectral responsivities across the encoding mask, individual channels reach their reliability limits at vastly different incident signal levels. Measurement reliability therefore depends on both exposure time and encoding channel, making it challenging for a single exposure to preserve spectral information in highlights and shadows simultaneously. Here, we demonstrate a physics-guided multi-exposure fusion framework that operates directly in the encoded measurement domain. An analytical reliability prior and learned spatially varying, channel-specific adjustments jointly determine adaptive fusion weights. Measurement-domain spectral-angle supervision further constrains relative channel responses for downstream spectral inversion. The set-wise formulation accommodates varying numbers and configurations of input exposures. We further implement the framework on a 9-channel broadband-encoded stochastic hyperspectral camera, incorporating full-field sensor-response characterization and channel-aware reliability gating. Simulated HDR benchmarks show lower reconstruction errors than representative fusion methods, while controlled spectral measurements and practical HDR scenes confirm improved spectral fidelity and extended usable dynamic range. Measurements using an optical-density target further establish a 16.0-dB increase in spectral reconstruction dynamic range relative to the best fixed single exposure.
tldr: This paper presents a physics-guided multi-exposure fusion framework for computational hyperspectral imaging that extends dynamic range by operating directly in the encoded measurement domain.
motivation: Computational hyperspectral imaging struggles with high-dynamic-range scenes because encoded measurements must remain within the linear-response range and above the noise floor, while unequal spectral responsivities cause channels to saturate or become unreliable at different signal levels.
method: The authors develop an adaptive fusion framework combining an analytical reliability prior with learned spatially varying, channel-specific adjustments, and use measurement-domain spectral-angle supervision for downstream spectral inversion on a 9-channel broadband-encoded stochastic hyperspectral camera.
result: Simulated HDR benchmarks show lower reconstruction errors than representative fusion methods, and experiments demonstrate a 16.0-dB increase in spectral reconstruction dynamic range relative to the best fixed single exposure.
conclusion: The proposed measurement-domain fusion approach improves spectral fidelity and extends usable dynamic range for computational hyperspectral imaging, though it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Stinging The Swarm: Extracting Attacker Intelligence From A Twin-Controller Ot Honeypot
authors: Joao Pedro de Carvalho Voltani Canyon Grey Dell'omo
abstract: ArXiv:2611.13406v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Autonomous language-model agents can drive industrial controllers over fieldbus protocols, probing a plant at machine speed and in coordinated swarms. We present Talos, an inline gate that judges every agent request to a controller in milliseconds and routes agents it flags as hostile to a device-faithful decoy -- a mirror twin of the real plant -- where their attack continues harmlessly and is read for intelligence. We evaluate the full pipeline (detect -> quarantine -> mirror -> extract) against 2,400 autonomous attacker agents, 600 in each of four tiers that escalate the attacker's effort to stay hidden, from no concealment to an explicit non-disclosure rule and a trained cover story. No write reached the real plant in any tier: the gate denies the damage path and a device-level envelope check backstops it, while unmapped registers are denied without exception and the gate still permits safe-direction stop commands. Decisions are model-driven in every tier with no inference timeouts, closing a common objection to small on-device judges. Beyond blocking, the pipeline reads the attacker. We find a behavioral structure along two axes -- how persistently an agent attacks and how much it discloses -- and show that the system has a capture channel for three of the four resulting regions: hardened, silent attackers escalate most and are read on the mirror; compliant, talkative attackers volunteer their identity to a diagnostic form before they are ever quarantined; only the paranoid, low-yield region resists both. Attacker identity fields are self-authored cover stories, but involuntary tells -- the self-reported toolchain fingerprint and the attacker's own list of targeted registers -- accumulate across the swarm into a high-confidence profile drawn from agents under explicit orders to stay silent. The gate, mirror, and harness are released under Apache 2.0 with a synthetic device family.
tldr: Talos is an inline honeypot gate that detects hostile autonomous LLM agents targeting OT controllers, quarantines them to a mirrored decoy plant, and extracts attacker intelligence.
motivation: Autonomous language-model agents can swarm industrial controllers at machine speed, creating a need for inline defenses that both block damage and gather intelligence from attackers.
method: The system judges each controller request in milliseconds, routes flagged agents to a device-faithful decoy, and analyzes their behavior across 2,400 attacker agents in four concealment tiers.
result: No write reached the real plant in any tier, and the pipeline extracted attacker profiles from involuntary tells for three of four behavioral regions, with only paranoid low-yield attackers resisting both capture channels.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a full detect-quarantine-mirror-extract pipeline for OT honeypots against LLM-driven attackers and releases the gate, mirror, and harness under Apache 2.0.

title: Model-Based Authoring Of Soc Simulation Exercises For Cybersecurity Education
authors: Felix H\"arer
abstract: ArXiv:2611.14227v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cybersecurity training and classroom exercises with a virtual Security Operations Center (SOC) combine alerts, evidence, timeline entries, learner tasks, and assessment items that must remain consistent across an evolving incident. This paper presents a model-based authoring method in which a technical and educational specification is used to construct an incident exercise model and a large language model (LLM) generates selected scenario text based on that model. The incident exercise model combines an incident model of events, objects, and evidence with an exercise orchestration model of SOC alerts, timeline entries, learner tasks, and assessment items. The method is implemented in a Virtual SOC prototype and evaluated using a phishing-to-ransomware reference exercise. Its incident exercise model contains eight incident events, eight incident objects, six evidence items, seven alerts in five batches, 13 timeline entries including 12 learner tasks, and five representative assessment items. GLM-5.3-generated alert descriptions are inserted and a separate validator checks references, ordering, evidence links, assessment completeness, and selected fixed fields. Validation is demonstrated with reference data, resulting in true-negative outcomes for valid data and true-positive outcomes for deliberately placed inconsistencies. The resulting exercise package is executable within the Virtual SOC learner environment. Overall, the evaluation indicates consistency across the involved model elements and establishes the feasibility of the model-based and generative approach.
tldr: The paper presents a model-based authoring method for cybersecurity SOC simulation exercises, using an incident exercise model and LLM-generated scenario text validated for internal consistency.
motivation: Cybersecurity training exercises require consistent alerts, evidence, timelines, tasks, and assessments across an evolving incident, which is difficult to author manually.
method: The author defines a combined incident model and exercise orchestration model, implements it in a Virtual SOC prototype, and uses an LLM to generate selected scenario text with a separate validator checking references, ordering, evidence links, and assessment completeness.
result: A phishing-to-ransomware reference exercise was constructed with eight events, eight objects, six evidence items, seven alerts, 13 timeline entries, 12 learner tasks, and five assessment items; validation produced true negatives for valid data and true positives for deliberately placed inconsistencies.
conclusion: The approach demonstrates feasibility and consistency for model-based generative authoring of executable SOC training exercises, but it is unrelated to quantum information science.

title: Reliability Analysis For Ground-Air Cooperative Wireless-Powered Internet-of-Things
authors: Xingyu Huang, Zhican Zhong, Yulei Wang, Yalin Liu, Yongqiang Cui, Di Bai
abstract: ArXiv:2611.12952v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Battery-constrained Internet of Things (IoT) devices face significant challenges in maintaining long-term uplink data collection, especially in network-limited scenarios. This paper investigates a Ground-Air cooperative Wireless-Powered IoT network (GA-WPIoT), where ground power beacons (GPBs) provide radio-frequency energy supply and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) serve as flexible aerial access points for IoT data collection. Unlike conventional UAV-enabled wireless-powered solutions, GA-WPIoT decouples energy transfer and data collection, reducing the hardware and energy burden of UAVs. To capture the device-level performance variations among IoT devices, we develop a stochastic geometry-based analytical framework, where UAVs are modeled by a Mat\'ern hard-core point process, IoT devices by a Poisson point process, and GPBs by a finite annular binomial point process. The conditional success probabilities of the GPB-device link (for energy transfer) and the device-UAV link (for data collection) are characterized, and device-level reliability distributions are obtained through the Meta-Distribution based analysis. Numerical results under suburban and urban environments reveal the impacts of UAV altitude and annular GPB deployment on reliability distributions, providing useful guidelines for GA-WPIoT.
tldr: A stochastic-geometry reliability analysis of a ground-air cooperative wireless-powered IoT network where ground power beacons supply RF energy and UAVs collect data.
motivation: Battery-constrained IoT devices struggle with long-term uplink data collection in network-limited settings, motivating architectures that decouple energy transfer from data collection to reduce UAV hardware and energy burden.
method: UAVs are modeled as a Matérn hard-core point process, IoT devices as a Poisson point process, and ground power beacons as a finite annular binomial point process; conditional success probabilities for the beacon-device energy link and device-UAV data link are derived, with device-level reliability distributions obtained via meta-distribution analysis.
result: Numerical results for suburban and urban environments quantify how UAV altitude and annular beacon deployment affect reliability distributions, yielding deployment guidelines.
conclusion: The GA-WPIoT framework and its analytical characterization provide design guidance for reliable wireless-powered IoT data collection, but the work is purely classical communication networking with no quantum information, thermodynamic, or quantum-network content.

title: State-constrained Optimal Control With The Theory Of Functional Connections: Squared Slacks And Junction Exponents
authors: Daniele Mortari Emmanuel Tr{\'e}lat (LJLL)
abstract: ArXiv:2611.13047v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For optimal control problems with an affine state constraint, we combine the theory of functional connections (TFC), which writes every function satisfying prescribed linear conditions as an explicit expression in terms of a free function, with the squared-slack substitution [MATH]. Every trial trajectory then satisfies the endpoint conditions and the path constraint identically. The accuracy depends on the regularity of the slack function at the junctions with a boundary arc. Along an optimal trajectory, the constraint residual vanishes like [MATH], where the junction exponent [MATH] is equal to the order [MATH] of the constraint if and only if the [MATH]-th derivative of the constraint jumps at the junction, and thus a single polynomial slack converges algebraically. The that we introduce, with unknown junction times and with residuals [MATH] on the free arcs, represents the optimal trajectory exactly and converges geometrically when the arcs are analytic. In a linear-quadratic class, an exact cost identity shows that the cost of every trial trajectory is an upper bound of the optimal cost. We compare both approaches with direct collocation and indirect shooting on the Bryson-Denham problem, on a rendezvous problem with an approach corridor and on the six-dimensional atmospheric reentry of a space shuttle with three state constraints.
tldr: The paper combines the theory of functional connections with a squared-slack substitution to enforce affine state constraints in optimal control problems, introducing junction exponents to characterize convergence of trial trajectories.
motivation: Standard direct methods for state-constrained optimal control struggle to enforce path constraints exactly and to represent the non-smooth behavior of the constraint at junctions with boundary arcs.
method: Trial trajectories are written via TFC so that endpoint and path constraints hold identically, with slack functions whose regularity at junctions is captured by the junction exponent; a variant with unknown junction times and residuals on free arcs is also introduced.
result: A single polynomial slack converges only algebraically, with the junction exponent equal to the constraint order iff the corresponding constraint derivative jumps; the proposed representation is exact and converges geometrically for analytic arcs, and an exact cost identity gives upper bounds in a linear-quadratic class, benchmarked against collocation and shooting on Bryson-Denham, rendezvous, and shuttle reentry problems.
conclusion: The TFC-based squared-slack framework provides accurate, constraint-satisfying trajectory representations and outperforms standard collocation and indirect shooting on several benchmark problems.

title: Convergence Of An Adaptive Multilevel Stochastic Galerkin Fem Driven By A Residual-based Error Estimator
authors: Alex Bespalov, Maximilian Brunner, Alexander Freiszlinger, Dirk Praetorius
abstract: ArXiv:2611.13145v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we analyze a residual-based a posteriori error estimation strategy and adaptive multilevel algorithms for a class of parametric elliptic PDEs, where the diffusion coefficient depends on countably many uncertainty parameters. Under a saturation assumption on the parametric approximation space, we propose a computable residual-based error estimator. We also introduce the notion of K-compatibility of finite element meshes, which ensures that only the triangulations with comparable mesh sizes are used, and incorporate this concept into the adaptive algorithm. We prove that the estimator is reliable and satisfies K-dependent stability and reduction properties. These results underpin our convergence analysis of the adaptive multilevel algorithm: we show that the algorithm drives both the a posteriori error estimator and the true approximation error to zero. Numerical experiments illustrate and confirm the theoretical findings.
tldr: The paper develops and proves convergence of an adaptive multilevel stochastic Galerkin finite element method for parametric elliptic PDEs with countably many random coefficients, driven by a computable residual-based a posteriori error estimator.
motivation: Parametric elliptic PDEs with high-dimensional uncertainty require efficient adaptive discretization strategies, but rigorous convergence guarantees for multilevel stochastic Galerkin schemes driven by residual-based estimators have been lacking.
method: The authors introduce a residual-based a posteriori error estimator under a saturation assumption on the parametric space plus a notion of K-compatibility of finite element meshes, and prove reliability, K-dependent stability, and reduction properties to underpin the convergence analysis.
result: The adaptive multilevel algorithm is shown to drive both the error estimator and the true approximation error to zero, with numerical experiments confirming the theoretical findings.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous convergence framework for adaptive multilevel stochastic Galerkin FEM in uncertainty quantification, though it is purely numerical analysis with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Effect Of Car-centric Social Norms On Traffic Congestion In A Compartmental Model Of Transit Mode Utilization
authors: Anastasia Bizyaeva Alia Valentine
abstract: ArXiv:2611.13265v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vehicle traffic congestion is a persistent feature of urban transportation systems around the world.Importantly, congestion is in part a consequence of human decision-making: car traffic is reduced when people choose modes of transportation such as metro trains, buses, or trams, over cars, and it is amplified when there is a persistent social bias towards driving. The underlying feedback loop in which traffic levels influence transportation mode choices, which in turn affect traffic levels themselves, is poorly understood and we study its consequences in the presented work using a compartmental modeling approach. We first consider a simplified model of only car traffic and show that it predicts a hysteresis between congested and uncongested states, which is consistent with broader literature on on traffic modeling. Next, we add buses and trains to the model as alternative transit modes, confirm the existence of hysteresis in this generalization, and derive the relative trip completion rates of each mode. Finally, to account for decision-making, we take the demand rates for the different transit modes to be dynamic, closing the feedback loop between mode choice and utilization. This redistributes demand for each mode of transportation, highlighting that traffic conditions may be a key aspect of mode choice.
